# majordom-integration-sdk

Models, protocols, and tooling for building [MajorDom](https://majordom.io) integrations.

An integration bridges an external protocol or platform (Matter, Zigbee, HomeKit, a vendor
cloud, …) into the MajorDom language. This SDK is the contract: the schemas, the
`AbstractController` framework, the device-repository protocol, discovery services, and a
standalone dev runner so you can build and test an integration **without a running Hub**.
The Hub itself depends on this same package — first-party integrations use no private
shortcut.

## Install

```sh
pip install majordom-integration-sdk
```

Requires Python 3.12+.

## Also a standalone IoT toolkit

You don't need MajorDom to get value from this package. `majordom_integration_sdk.discovery`
ships three fully working, standardized device-discovery services you can drop into **any**
async Python project:

- **Zeroconf / mDNS** (`ZeroconfDiscoveryService`) — browse Bonjour/mDNS services with a
  clean listener protocol, and — unusually — **reliable disappearance tracking**: it augments
  raw zeroconf with an active cache-poll + confirm-evict loop so you get accurate "device
  went away" events, not just arrivals.
- **SSDP / UPnP** (`SSDPDiscoveryService`) — flexible, per-listener **configurable** search
  targets and refresh behavior over raw sockets, without dragging in a full UPnP stack.
- **BLE** (`BLEDiscoveryService`) — a uniform listener interface over Bleak for advertisement
  scanning.

All three share one `register(listener, …) → cancel` shape, run standalone (each module has a
runnable `__main__` demo), and are a solid reference for implementing **standardized
interfaces over messy IoT protocols** even if you never touch MajorDom. The
`AbstractController` framework and the `DeviceRepositoryProtocol` + in-memory/SQLite
implementations are equally reusable as a small, typed device-modelling toolkit.

## Documentation

Full integration-author docs — models, the controller lifecycle, storing data, discovery,
and a worked example — live at **[docs.majordom.io](https://docs.majordom.io/device-integration)**.

The fastest way to start a new integration is the
[integration-template](https://github.com/MajorDom-Systems/integration-template) repository
(**Use this template → Create a new repository**).

## License

See [LICENSE](LICENSE). For commercial licensing or partnership inquiries, contact us via
[parker-industries.org/partnership](https://parker-industries.org/partnership).

---

## Development

Setup:

```sh
poetry install && poetry run poe install
```

This installs dependencies and the pre-commit hook that runs `poe check`.

| Task | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `poe install` | Install deps and register the pre-commit hook |
| `poe check` | Full quality pipeline (ruff, ty, pytest, poetry build/check) |
| `poe check --ci` | Same, plus `git diff --exit-code` |

Two long-lived branches: `develop` (integration branch, all work lands here) and `master`
(protected, released). Releases are cut from `develop` via **Actions → Release**; see
[ParkerIndustries/workflows](https://github.com/ParkerIndustries/workflows) for the CI/CD.

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/__init__.py
================================================================================
"""MajorDom Integration SDK — models, protocols, and tooling for building integrations.

Public submodules:

- ``majordom_integration_sdk.schemas``       — the wire protocol (pydantic models shared with the Hub)
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.controller``    — ``AbstractController`` + its ``ControllerOutput``
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.platform``      — ``Platform``: the host every peripheral runs on, as ``self.platform``
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals``   — ``Peripheral``, ``Need``/``Endpoint``, ``Service``: what runs around it
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities``  — the contracts of in-process peripherals: BLE router, DNS-SD, SSDP
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.repository``    — ``DeviceRepositoryProtocol`` + in-memory / SQLite implementations
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.testing``       — shared test doubles for integration test suites
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.dev``           — standalone runner for developing an integration without the Hub
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.runtime``       — runs peripherals and binds their needs (the ``runtime`` extra)
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.errors``        — errors an integration raises for the Hub to act on
- ``majordom_integration_sdk.files``         — ``read_json`` / ``write_json``: files kept whole, for their owner alone

The names an integration author reaches for most are re-exported here for convenience, e.g.
``from majordom_integration_sdk import AbstractController, Device``.
"""

from importlib.metadata import version

from majordom_integration_sdk.controller import AbstractController, ControllerOutput, IntegrationError
from majordom_integration_sdk.errors import MissingCredentialsError
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import (
    STABLE_RUN,
    ComposeService,
    Endpoint,
    Need,
    NoSettings,
    Peripheral,
    PeripheralChange,
    PeripheralOutput,
    Peripherals,
    Service,
    SettingsExtraField,
    UsbDriver,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.platform import Platform
from majordom_integration_sdk.repository import (
    DeviceRepositoryMemory,
    DeviceRepositoryProtocol,
    SqliteDeviceRepository,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.command import DeviceCommand
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.credentials import ProvidedCredentials, WifiCredentials
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, Discovery, Parameter
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.event import DeviceParameterChange, Event

__version__ = version("majordom-integration-sdk")

__all__ = [
    "AbstractController",
    "ControllerOutput",
    "IntegrationError",
    "Platform",
    "DeviceRepositoryProtocol",
    "DeviceRepositoryMemory",
    "SqliteDeviceRepository",
    "DeviceCommand",
    "Device",
    "Discovery",
    "Parameter",
    "ProvidedCredentials",
    "Event",
    "DeviceParameterChange",
    "MissingCredentialsError",
    "Need",
    "Endpoint",
    "Peripheral",

    "Peripherals",

================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/capabilities/ble.py
================================================================================
"""The ``ble/router`` contract: one Bluetooth LE router that hears every radio and reaches every device.

Integrations need it as `BLE_ROUTER` and get it at ``self.peripherals.instance(BLE_ROUTER)``; never raw
Bluetooth, which the router holds. Its sources are the radios the runtime binds to it (``ble/bluez`` adapters,
``ble/silabs-cpc-hci``, ``ble/esphome-proxy`` nodes an integration brings along): `BLESource`s.

Listeners register `BLEMatcher`s and hear about matching devices whichever source saw them.
`BLERouter.connect` opens a GATT connection through the source that hears the device best;
`BLERouter.exclusive` leases that one source to a device for as long as pairing it takes.
Credentials go to a device only over a link a `SecureChannel` (`ble_security`) has secured first.

bleak's advertisement types describe what is heard; this module imports them for type checking only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol, runtime_checkable
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.need import Need

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from bleak.backends.device import BLEDevice
    from bleak.backends.scanner import AdvertisementData

type OnAdvertisement = Callable[[BLEDevice, AdvertisementData], None]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BLEMatcher:
    """What a listener wants to hear about; every field that is set must match. A manufacturer id alone selects
    protocols that advertise no service UUID, e.g. HomeKit (HAP-BLE) accessories by Apple's company id."""

    service_uuid: UUID | None = None  # advertised as a service or in the service data
    service_data_uuid: UUID | None = None  # in the service data only (what the listener reads)
    manufacturer_id: int | None = None
    manufacturer_data_start: bytes = b""
    local_name_prefix: str | None = None

    def matches(self, adv: AdvertisementData) -> bool:
        if self.service_uuid and str(self.service_uuid) not in {*adv.service_uuids, *adv.service_data}:
            return False
        if self.service_data_uuid and str(self.service_data_uuid) not in adv.service_data:
            return False
        if self.manufacturer_id is not None:
            data = adv.manufacturer_data.get(self.manufacturer_id)
            if data is None or not bytes(data).startswith(self.manufacturer_data_start):
                return False
        return not self.local_name_prefix or (adv.local_name or "").startswith(self.local_name_prefix)


@dataclass
class BLEDiscoveryInfo:
    device: BLEDevice
    advertisement: AdvertisementData
    source: str = "local"  # the source that hears it best: "hci0", "esphome:<mac>", …
    rssi: int | None = None  # as that source hears it
    last_seen: float = 0.0  # monotonic


class BLEDiscoveryListener(Protocol):
    async def ble_did_discover_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo): ...
    async def ble_did_update_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo): ...
    async def ble_did_remove_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo): ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GattCharacteristic:
    uuid: str
    handle: int
    properties: tuple[str, ...]  # "read", "write", "write-without-response", "notify", "indicate", …


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GattService:
    uuid: str
    handle: int
    characteristics: tuple[GattCharacteristic, ...]


class BLEConnection(Protocol):
    """An open GATT connection; characteristics are addressed by handle."""

    @property
    def mtu(self) -> int: ...
    async def services(self) -> list[GattService]: ...
    async def read(self, handle: int) -> bytes: ...
    async def write(self, handle: int, data: bytes, is_response_needed: bool = True): ...
    async def start_notify(self, handle: int, callback: Callable[[bytes], None]): ...
    async def stop_notify(self, handle: int): ...
    async def disconnect(self): ...


@runtime_checkable
class PairableBLEConnection(BLEConnection, Protocol):
    """A connection that can encrypt its link by pairing (LE Secure Connections where both ends support it)."""

    async def pair(self):
        """Pairs "Just Works", encrypting the link. Raises `BLEPairingError`."""
        ...

    async def unpair(self):
        """Forgets the bond; the link may drop."""
        ...


class BLESource(Protocol):
    """A radio that hears advertisements and can connect to devices: a local adapter or a proxy. Optional
    attributes the router reads: a true ``is_pairable`` when its connections are `PairableBLEConnection`s,
    ``free_slots``, the connections it can still open (a proxy has a few), None when it can't tell, and a true
    ``is_loss_reported`` when its radio going away is reported otherwise (an ESPHome node's API connection drops, and
    the integration takes the source away): the router then never restarts it for hearing nothing for a while."""

    name: str

    async def start(self, on_advertisement: OnAdvertisement): ...
    async def stop(self): ...
    async def connect(self, address: str, on_disconnect: Callable[[], None]) -> BLEConnection: ...


@runtime_checkable
class PausableBLESource(BLESource, Protocol):
    """A source that can stop hearing without letting go of its radio, e.g. a proxy whose connections only
    work while it stays subscribed; a lease pauses one rather than stopping it."""

    async def pause_scanning(self): ...
    async def resume_scanning(self): ...


@runtime_checkable
class ScanModeBLESource(BLESource, Protocol):
    """A source that scans passively (every advertiser, the listeners' matchers choose) or actively (asking for the
    scan responses that often carry the name): the router switches it for a pairing window. Called before `start`
    too; a running source applies a change itself."""

    async def set_scan_mode(self, is_active: bool): ...


class BLEBusyError(ConnectionError):
    """Every source that hears the device is leased to someone else."""


class BLEPairingError(ConnectionError):
    """The link could not be encrypted: pairing failed, or no source that hears the device can pair."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BLELease:
    """One source held for one device: it doesn't scan, and only the holder connects through it."""

    address: str
    source: str
    owner: str
    _source: BLESource = field(repr=False)

    async def connect(self, on_disconnect: Callable[[], None] = lambda: None) -> BLEConnection:
        return await self._source.connect(self.address, on_disconnect)


class BLERouter(Protocol):
    """Bluetooth LE across all sources: discovery for listeners, GATT connections on demand."""

    def register(self, listener: BLEDiscoveryListener, matchers: Iterable[BLEMatcher | UUID]) -> Callable[[], None]:
        """Registers a listener for BLE devices matching any of ``matchers`` (a UUID matches that service).
        `ble_did_discover_device` is called when a device first matches, `ble_did_update_device` when its
        advertisement changes, `ble_did_remove_device` when no source has heard it for a while; devices heard
        before it registered are new to it. Returns a cancel function — call it on stop to deregister."""
        ...

    async def connect(self, address: str, on_disconnect: Callable[[], None] = lambda: None) -> BLEConnection:
        """Opens a GATT connection to ``address`` through the source hearing it best, falling back to the others;
        leased sources are skipped. ``on_disconnect`` is called when the connection drops."""
        ...

    def exclusive(
        self, address: str, *, owner: str, timeout: float = 30, wait: float = 1, is_pairing_needed: bool = False
    ) -> contextlib.AbstractAsyncContextManager[BLELease]:
        """Leases the source hearing ``address`` best to ``owner`` (e.g. while pairing it): that source pauses
        scanning and others' connects avoid it; the rest keep going. A leased source is waited for ``wait`` seconds
        before the next best is tried, round after round, until ``timeout`` raises `BLEBusyError`. With
        ``is_pairing_needed``, only sources that can pair are leased (`BLEPairingError` when none hears it)."""
        ...

    async def scan_actively(self, duration: float):
        """Scans actively for ``duration`` seconds (a pairing window): names often come only in the scan
        responses a passive scan never asks for."""
        ...

    def devices(self) -> list[BLEDiscoveryInfo]:
        """Every device heard recently, as the source hearing it best sees it."""
        ...


BLE_ROUTER = Need[BLERouter]("ble", ["router"])  # optional: dataclasses.replace(it, is_required=False)


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/capabilities/ble_security.py
================================================================================
"""Secure channels: how credentials (a Wi-Fi password, a Thread network key) are protected on a BLE connection before
they are written to a device. An integration picks one per device and opens it on the leased connection::

    async with ble.exclusive(address, owner=OWNER, is_pairing_needed=channel.is_pairing_needed) as lease:
        async with channel.secure(await lease.connect()) as connection:
            await connection.write(rpc, credentials)

`LESecureConnections` encrypts the link by pairing. "Just Works" pairing, all a headless Hub can do, stops passive
sniffing but not an active man in the middle during the pairing itself. A channel that
authenticates at the application layer (e.g. Improv's proposed SPAKE2+ setup code) would yield a connection that
encrypts the frames it writes instead, and works through any proxy.
"""

import contextlib
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from typing import Protocol

from .ble import BLEConnection, BLEPairingError, PairableBLEConnection

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class SecureChannel(Protocol):
    is_pairing_needed: bool  # lease a source that can pair: `BLERouter.exclusive(..., is_pairing_needed=...)`

    def secure(self, connection: BLEConnection) -> contextlib.AbstractAsyncContextManager[BLEConnection]:
        """The connection to write credentials through, secured; raises `BLEPairingError` (fail closed)."""
        ...


class LESecureConnections:
    """Pairs before anything is written: the link is encrypted, or nothing is yielded. The device decides LE Secure
    Connections over legacy pairing (firmware built for it accepts nothing else). It unpairs once done, as the
    pairing served only the setup, unless ``is_pairing_kept``."""

    is_pairing_needed = True

    def __init__(self, is_pairing_kept: bool = False):
        self._is_pairing_kept = is_pairing_kept

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def secure(self, connection: BLEConnection) -> AsyncGenerator[BLEConnection]:
        if not isinstance(connection, PairableBLEConnection):
            raise BLEPairingError("This Bluetooth source can't pair, so it can't encrypt the link")
        await connection.pair()
        try:
            yield connection
        finally:
            if not self._is_pairing_kept:
                with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                    await connection.unpair()


class Unsecured:
    """Writes over the link as it is: only for firmware that can't pair, chosen explicitly."""

    is_pairing_needed = False

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def secure(self, connection: BLEConnection) -> AsyncGenerator[BLEConnection]:
        logger.warning("Writing credentials over an unencrypted Bluetooth link")
        yield connection

"""The ``upnp/ssdp`` contract: hearing UPnP devices and services over SSDP.

Integrations need it as `UPNP_SSDP` and get the runtime's listener at ``self.peripherals.instance(UPNP_SSDP)``: an
`SSDP`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.need import Need


@dataclass
class SSDPDiscoveryInfo:
    addr: str
    host: str | None
    search_target: str | None
    service_name: str | None
    server: str | None
    cache_control: str | None
    location: str | None
    response: dict[str, str]


class SSDPDiscoveryListener(Protocol):
    async def ssdp_did_discover_service(self, ssdp: SSDP, info: SSDPDiscoveryInfo): ...
    async def ssdp_did_update_service(self, ssdp: SSDP, info: SSDPDiscoveryInfo): ...
    async def ssdp_did_remove_service(self, ssdp: SSDP, info: SSDPDiscoveryInfo): ...


class SSDP(Protocol):
    def register(
        self,
        listener: SSDPDiscoveryListener,
        search_target: str,
        mcast_group: str = "239.255.255.250",
        port: int = 1900,
    ) -> Callable[[], None]:
        """Calls ``listener`` about what answers ``search_target`` (``"ssdp:all"``, a device or service type) as it
        comes, changes and goes. Returns a cancel function — call it on stop to deregister."""
        ...


UPNP_SSDP = Need[SSDP]("upnp", ["ssdp"])  # optional: dataclasses.replace(it, is_required=False)


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/capabilities/zeroconf.py
================================================================================
"""The ``mdns/zeroconf`` contract: browsing DNS-SD services over mDNS.

Integrations need it as `ZEROCONF` and get the runtime's browser at ``self.peripherals.instance(ZEROCONF)``: a
`Zeroconf`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.need import Need

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from zeroconf.asyncio import AsyncZeroconf


@dataclass
class ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo:
    """
    * `type_`: fully qualified service type name
    * `name`: fully qualified service name
    * `port`: port that the service runs on
    * `weight`: weight of the service
    * `priority`: priority of the service
    * `properties`: dictionary of properties as raw bytes. Keys with `None` values are value-less attributes.
    * `decoded_properties`: `properties` decoded to `str` — use this for most integrations.
    * `text`: raw TXT record bytes — use only if you need to parse the record manually.
    * `server`: fully qualified name for service host (defaults to name)
    * `host_ttl`: ttl used for A/SRV records
    * `other_ttl`: ttl used for PTR/TXT records
    * `addresses` and `parsed_addresses`: List of IP addresses (either as bytes, network byte order,
        or in parsed form as text; at most one of those parameters can be provided)
    * interface_index: scope_id or zone_id for IPv6 link-local addresses i.e. an identifier of the interface
        where the peer is connected to
    """

    type_: str
    name: str
    server: str | None
    port: int | None
    addresses: list[bytes] | None
    parsed_addresses: list[str] | None
    weight: int | None
    priority: int | None
    properties: dict[bytes, bytes | None]
    decoded_properties: dict[str, str | None]
    text: bytes
    host_ttl: int | None
    other_ttl: int | None
    interface_index: int | None

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(other, ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo):
            return NotImplemented
        # exclude host_ttl / other_ttl — they change on every re-announcement
        return (
            self.type_ == other.type_
            and self.name == other.name
            and self.server == other.server
            and self.port == other.port
            and self.addresses == other.addresses
            and self.parsed_addresses == other.parsed_addresses
            and self.weight == other.weight
            and self.priority == other.priority
            and self.properties == other.properties
            and self.text == other.text
            and self.interface_index == other.interface_index
        )


class ZeroconfDiscoveryListener(Protocol):
    async def zeroconf_did_discover_service(self, zeroconf: Zeroconf, info: ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo): ...
    async def zeroconf_did_update_service(self, zeroconf: Zeroconf, info: ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo): ...
    async def zeroconf_did_remove_service(self, zeroconf: Zeroconf, type_: str, name: str):
        """Fired on mDNS goodbye packets (TTL=0) or when a silent departure is confirmed:
        A/AAAA records expired (~120s TTL) and a follow-up async_request got no response.
        For faster detection, implement liveness checks at the pairing/connection layer."""
        ...


class Zeroconf(Protocol):
    def register(self, listener: ZeroconfDiscoveryListener, services: set[str]) -> Callable[[], None]:
        """Calls ``listener`` about the services of the given types (``"_hap._tcp.local."``) as they come, change
        and go. Returns a cancel function — call it on stop to deregister."""
        ...

    @property
    def async_zeroconf(self) -> AsyncZeroconf | None:
        """The zeroconf instance it browses with, for libraries that take one (aiohomekit); None until it starts."""
        ...


ZEROCONF = Need[Zeroconf]("mdns", ["zeroconf"])  # optional: dataclasses.replace(it, is_required=False)
