# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/ble_proxy.py
================================================================================
"""Bluetooth sources integrations lend the runtime's router."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities.ble import BLESource
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Endpoint
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.peripheral import Peripheral


class BLEProxy(Peripheral):
    """A Bluetooth source an integration brings along while it has it, e.g. an ESPHome node's proxy as
    ``ble/esphome-proxy``: the router binds it and hears through ``source``. Add one to what you provide when the source
    connects, remove it when it goes, and tell your ``output`` each time (``controller_did_change_provided``); they go
    when you stop. ``name`` is what it is known by after you, ``esphome/<name>``: the source's name by default, else
    e.g. the node's Bluetooth MAC.
    """

    def __init__(self, source: BLESource, name: str | None = None, dialect: str = "esphome-proxy"):
        self.name, self.source, self.dialect = name or source.name, source, dialect

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return [Endpoint("ble", self.dialect, self.source.name, instance=self.source)]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/endpoint.py
================================================================================
"""What peripherals provide, and what a need is bound to."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Endpoint:
    """What a peripheral provides — a radio, a service, the host, an in-process provider — and, once bound, what the
    peripheral that needs it uses.

    A radio firmware's ``url`` may hold ``{device}``, the stick's path; a service's ``{ports.<name>}``.
    ``params`` says how to talk to it, e.g. a serial port's ``baud`` and ``flow_control`` as the radio's
    firmware sets them; a service reads them as ``{peripherals.<family>.params[baud]}``. The params a service
    provides render like its compose, telling its consumers what it got: ``{"adapter": "{peripherals.ble.url}"}``.

    ``instance`` carries an in-process peripheral itself (the runtime's Bluetooth router, a DNS-SD browser, an
    ESPHome node's Bluetooth source); ``url`` still names it, and two endpoints are the same when all but the
    instance match.
    """

    family: str
    dialect: str = ""
    url: str = ""
    is_shared: bool = False  # several consumers may bind it (one Thread network); otherwise exactly one
    params: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict, hash=False)
    instance: Any = field(default=None, hash=False, compare=False, repr=False)


type Bound = Endpoint | list[Endpoint]  # what a need is bound to: a list for an ``is_many`` need


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PeripheralChange:
    """A bound need moved: ``after`` is None when it was lost, ``before`` is None when it (re)appeared."""

    family: str
    before: Bound | None
    after: Bound | None


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/need.py
================================================================================
"""What a peripheral requires from its environment."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Endpoint


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Need[T = Any]:
    """A dependency something else must provide, as ``family`` and the ``dialects`` it speaks; ``T`` types the
    in-process peripheral it binds, read back with ``self.peripherals.instance(need)``: ``Need[BLERouter]``.

    The runtime binds it to an `Endpoint` and hands that over in the peripheral's `Peripherals`, to a controller as
    ``self.peripherals.endpoint(<family>)`` and to a `Service` as ``{peripherals.<family>.url}``. An ``is_many`` need
    binds every matching endpoint that is free, as a list: a Bluetooth router hears through every radio it is given.
    """

    family: str
    dialects: Sequence[str] = ()  # empty: any dialect of the family
    is_required: bool = True
    is_many: bool = False

    def accepts(self, endpoint: Endpoint) -> bool:
        return endpoint.family == self.family and (not self.dialects or endpoint.dialect in self.dialects)


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/peripheral.py
================================================================================
"""The one protocol for everything around an integration, and how a peripheral talks to whatever runs it."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from types import MappingProxyType
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Protocol, cast

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Bound, Endpoint, PeripheralChange
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.need import Need

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.platform import Platform

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

START_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds a start may take to serve by default, else it failed
# seconds of running that clear a peripheral's failures in a row; an integration's outage ends once a reconnect held as
# long (a server that sends its nodes and drops every time is reported)
STABLE_RUN = 300


class NoSettings(BaseModel):
    """The settings of a peripheral without options: it takes none."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class PeripheralOutput(Protocol):
    """What a peripheral tells whatever runs it, through its ``output``, delegate style like `ControllerOutput`: what
    changed on its own (a stick plugged in, a node connected), what it learned, and that it stopped or failed. The
    runtime gives every peripheral it runs the same output; a controller reports through `ControllerOutput` instead.

    Awaiting a call returns once the runtime acted on it, e.g. stopped what used a radio about to be flashed. From
    inside ``start``, ``stop`` or a hook, or a task that call awaits (a ``TaskGroup``'s), it returns at once: the
    runtime acts when that call returns. It acts in a task of its own, so a call from a task the peripheral keeps
    running, which its ``stop`` cancels before awaiting it, is fine: that task just ends.
    """

    async def peripheral_did_change_provided(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        """Its ``provides`` or the peripherals it brings along changed."""
        ...

    async def peripheral_did_learn(self, peripheral: Peripheral, facts: Mapping[str, Any]):
        """`Platform` facts it read from what it runs or talks to, e.g. a border router's Thread network: they replace
        the platform's, and every peripheral that runs hears it (``platform_facts_did_change``). A name the platform
        holds no fact of is left out (logged)."""
        ...

    async def peripheral_did_stop(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        """It stopped by itself, gracefully: it is stopped (``stop`` releases what it holds) and waits until one of its
        needs changes (goes and comes back, or moves) or the user restarts it."""
        ...

    async def peripheral_did_fail(self, peripheral: Peripheral, reason: str):
        """It can't go on, ``reason`` saying why to the user: it is stopped and started again after each of the
        runtime's retry delays, then failed until the user restarts it. Told from inside ``start``, that start
        fails."""
        ...


class LoggingPeripheralOutput:
    """Nothing runs the peripheral (library mode, a test): what it tells is logged."""

    async def peripheral_did_change_provided(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        log.info(f"{peripheral.key} changed what it provides")

    async def peripheral_did_learn(self, peripheral: Peripheral, facts: Mapping[str, Any]):
        log.info(f"{peripheral.key} learned {', '.join(facts)}")

    async def peripheral_did_stop(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        log.info(f"{peripheral.key} stopped by itself")

    async def peripheral_did_fail(self, peripheral: Peripheral, reason: str):
        log.error(f"{peripheral.key} failed: {reason}")


class Peripherals:
    """What a peripheral's needs are bound to, by family: an `Endpoint`, or a list of them for an ``is_many`` need.

    A runtime hands a new one over before ``start`` and whenever the bindings change; in library mode hand it yours:
    ``controller.peripherals = Peripherals({"mdns": zeroconf.endpoint})``.
    """

    def __init__(self, bound: Mapping[str, Bound] | None = None):
        self.bound: Mapping[str, Bound] = MappingProxyType(dict(bound or {}))

    def endpoint(self, family: str) -> Endpoint:
        """The endpoint bound to the need of ``family``; KeyError while it is unbound."""
        bound = self.bound[family]
        if isinstance(bound, list):
            raise TypeError(f"The {family} need binds many endpoints: use endpoints({family!r})")
        return bound

    def endpoints(self, family: str) -> list[Endpoint]:
        """Every endpoint bound to the need of ``family``; empty while it is unbound."""
        bound = self.bound.get(family, [])
        return [bound] if isinstance(bound, Endpoint) else bound

    def instance[T](self, need: Need[T]) -> T | None:
        """The in-process peripheral bound to ``need``, typed by it, e.g. the Bluetooth router; None while unbound."""
        return self.endpoint(need.family).instance if need.family in self.bound else None


class Peripheral[S: BaseModel = Any](Protocol):
    """Anything around an integration that needs and/or provides capabilities: a USB radio, soldered hardware, the
    host's Bluetooth adapters and network, a container, an in-process provider (the Bluetooth router, Zeroconf, SSDP),
    an integration itself, an ESPHome node's Bluetooth proxy. Only the construction differs.

    It ``needs`` capabilities, ``provides`` endpoints and the peripherals it brings along, and finds what its needs
    are bound to in ``peripherals``. A runtime (`majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.Runtime`) runs every peripheral it is
    given by one rule: one that isn't disabled or failed runs while whatever brought it along does, while something
    that runs binds it if it ``is_on_demand``, and once every required need is bound to a provider that runs. A
    required need that can't be bound keeps it waiting, with the reason; one lost later stops it until it is back. An
    optional need is handed over once its provider runs, as it appears.

    Subclass it for the defaults. The runtime sets ``platform`` (the host, the same for every peripheral: its facts,
    and a documents folder per peripheral), ``output`` (what it tells), ``peripherals``, ``contributor`` and
    ``settings``, its options validated by its ``Settings``. Declare them as a nested ``class Settings(BaseModel)``
    named as the type parameter, which types ``settings``: ``class Radio(Peripheral["Radio.Settings"])``. Without,
    they are `NoSettings`; a bare ``Peripheral`` is one of any settings. A field marked read-only in its JSON schema,
    ``channel: int = Field(11, json_schema_extra={Extra.read_only: True})``, shows what the peripheral fills in itself
    (``self.settings.channel = 25``): the user sees it, and an update to another value is refused. It is never kept:
    until the peripheral fills it in again, it holds its default. One marked write-only,
    ``network_key: str = Field("", json_schema_extra={Extra.write_only: True})``, is the reverse: the user sets it,
    and the host never shows it (the Hub never reads it back), so an update that leaves it out keeps it. ``Extra`` is
    `SettingsExtraField`: never spell a keyword out.
    """

    name: str  # what it is shown by
    contributor: Peripheral | None = None  # what brought it along
    needs: Sequence[Need] = ()
    is_on_demand: bool = False  # runs only while something that runs binds it: containers, in-process providers
    start_timeout: float = START_TIMEOUT
    settings: S
    platform: Platform  # the host it runs on
    output: PeripheralOutput = LoggingPeripheralOutput()  # what it tells whatever runs it
    peripherals: Peripherals = Peripherals()  # what its needs are bound to

    @property
    def Settings(self) -> type[S]:
        """The model of its options; `NoSettings` when it has none. Read-only, so a nested class may override it."""
        return cast(type[S], NoSettings)

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        """What it is known, kept and disabled by where it runs, unique there and stable across restarts: its name,
        after its contributor's key for one brought along (``usb/<stick>``, ``esphome/<node>``)."""
        return f"{self.contributor.key}/{self.name}" if self.contributor else self.name

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint | Peripheral]:
        """What it serves to the others' needs, and the peripherals it brings along while it runs: the USB scanner a
        radio per stick, ESPHome a Bluetooth proxy per node. When it changes on its own, tell ``output``."""
        return ()

    async def start(self):
        """Set up what it serves, and return once it serves: what needs it starts then. Raising, or taking longer than
        its ``start_timeout``, has the runtime stop it, try again later (``RETRY_DELAYS``), then give up."""
        return

    async def stop(self):
        """Release everything it holds; what it brought along goes with it. It also follows a start that failed or was
        cut short: leave the object clean for the next ``start``, with nothing in flight taking resources after it."""
        return

    async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change: PeripheralChange) -> bool:
        """A bound need was lost, appeared or moved while it runs; its ``peripherals`` already hold the new binding.

        Return True when handled in place (Matter keeps working over IP without Thread); False, the default, restarts
        it. A required need that is lost stops it instead, without asking.
        """
        return False

    async def settings_did_change(self, before: S) -> bool:
        """Its ``settings`` changed while it runs. True when applied in place; False, the default, restarts it."""
        return False

    async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before: Platform) -> bool:
        """The host's facts changed (region, Wi-Fi, Thread network) while it runs; ``platform`` holds the new ones.
        True, the default, when they don't concern it or were applied in place; False restarts it."""
        return True


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/service.py
================================================================================
"""Companion servers an integration provides, run as containers while something uses them."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal, Protocol, TypedDict

from pydantic import BaseModel

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Endpoint, PeripheralChange
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.need import Need
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.peripheral import NoSettings, Peripheral

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.platform import Platform


class Healthcheck(TypedDict, total=False):
    test: list[str]
    interval: str
    timeout: str
    start_period: str
    retries: int


class ComposeService(TypedDict, total=False):
    """A Docker Compose service definition, the keys services use typed (a typo fails type checking, not the start);
    another key goes here first. Its strings are templates: see `Service`."""

    image: str
    build: str
    command: list[str]
    entrypoint: list[str]
    environment: dict[str, str]
    volumes: list[str]
    devices: list[str]
    tmpfs: list[str]
    network_mode: Literal["host", "bridge", "none"]
    userns_mode: Literal["host"]
    user: str
    privileged: bool
    hostname: str
    cap_add: list[str]
    cap_drop: list[str]
    group_add: list[str]
    healthcheck: Healthcheck


class ServiceHost(Protocol):
    """What runs a `Service`'s container, bound to its ``container`` need: the runtime's `Compose`."""

    def provided(self, service: Service) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        """Its ``provides`` rendered: the host ports it got, the params it renders."""
        ...

    async def up(self, service: Service):
        """Run its container; return once it serves."""
        ...

    async def down(self, service: Service): ...

    def is_current(self, service: Service) -> bool:
        """Whether its container still runs what it would render now."""
        ...


CONTAINER_HOST = Need[ServiceHost]("container", ["compose"])  # what every service needs


class Service[S: BaseModel = Any](Peripheral[S]):
    """A companion server an integration provides, such as Matter's matterjs-server: a container that runs only while
    something that runs is bound to one of its endpoints. The integration lists it next to its controller, which
    `Need`s what it provides.

    ``compose`` is its Docker Compose service definition (image, environment, volumes, …); its strings may hold
    ``{data}`` (its own documents folder), ``{peripherals.<family>.url}``, ``{settings.<field>}``,
    ``{platform.<fact>}`` (``{platform.region}``), ``{host.interface|uid|gid|listen_address}`` and ``{ports.<name>}``.
    A format spec turns a value into text: ``{x:!text}`` renders ``text`` when ``x`` is empty, ``{x:?text}`` when it
    isn't; a list item that renders empty is left out, so
    ``"volumes": ["{peripherals.ble.url:?/run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro}"]`` mounts D-Bus only while an adapter is bound. One
    on the host network (``network_mode: host``) listens on ``{host.listen_address}``: loopback unless the host opens
    its services to the LAN for a lab harness.
    The ``params`` of the ``provides`` endpoints render the same way, which is how a consumer learns what its service
    got: ``params={"adapter": "{peripherals.ble.url}"}``. ``settings`` is the model of its options, its ``Settings``.

    ``ports`` names the host ports it listens on, each with the port it *prefers*, not a fixed one: the runtime uses it
    when free, else assigns another (45800-45999), keeps the choice across restarts, and fills ``{ports.<name>}`` in
    ``compose`` and in the ``provides`` URLs. Integrations never read a port: they connect through
    ``self.peripherals.endpoint(<family>).url``.

    Its start returns once its container runs, its ports answer, `provision` finished and `is_healthy` says so. A
    change of what its needs are bound to or of the platform's facts recreates it only when it renders otherwise.
    Subclass it to hook in: `provision` sets up what it runs, `is_healthy` checks more; a ``start`` of your own may tell
    what it learned once it serves (``self.output.peripheral_did_learn``).
    """

    is_on_demand = True
    start_timeout: float = 30 * 60  # its first start pulls its image

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        compose: ComposeService,
        needs: Sequence[Need] = (),
        provides: Sequence[Endpoint] = (),
        settings: type[S] = NoSettings,  # ty: ignore[invalid-parameter-default]  (none: it takes none)
        ports: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,  # name -> PREFERRED host port; see the docstring
    ):
        self.name, self.compose, self.needs, self.templates = name, compose, [*needs, CONTAINER_HOST], provides
        self.settings_model, self.ports = settings, ports or {}

    @property
    def Settings(self) -> type[S]:
        return self.settings_model

    @property
    def host(self) -> ServiceHost | None:
        """The container host its need is bound to."""
        return self.peripherals.instance(CONTAINER_HOST)

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return self.host.provided(self) if self.host else self.templates

    async def start(self):
        if not self.host:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"Nothing runs containers here: run {self.name} yourself and pin what it provides"
            )
        await self.host.up(self)

    async def stop(self):
        if self.host:
            await self.host.down(self)

    async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change: PeripheralChange) -> bool:
        """Its container is recreated only when it would render otherwise now, or on another container host."""
        return change.family != CONTAINER_HOST.family and self.host is not None and self.host.is_current(self)

    async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before: Platform) -> bool:
        """Its container is recreated only when it would render otherwise now."""
        return self.host.is_current(self) if self.host else True

    async def provision(self, endpoint: Endpoint):
        """Set up one of its endpoints once it answers, e.g. form a network. Called each time its container is
        (re)created, cancelled when it stops: keep it idempotent."""
        return

    async def is_healthy(self) -> bool:
        """A check of its own on top of its ports answering; asked until it says yes."""
        return True

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"{type(self).__name__}({self.name!r})"


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/usb.py
================================================================================
"""Drivers that recognise USB devices for the runtime's USB scanner."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, ClassVar

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Endpoint
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.peripheral import Peripheral

USB_DRIVER = "usb-driver"  # the family a driver provides itself as, to the scanners that need every driver


class UsbDriver(Peripheral):
    """One kind of USB device: recognises which firmware a device runs and says what each firmware serves.

    The scanner asks its own drivers first, then the ones integrations provide next to their controller: Zigbee's
    tells the radios only zigpy knows apart. ``firmwares`` maps a firmware to what it serves: ``{device}`` in a URL is
    the device's path, ``params`` its serial settings (soldered hardware may wire them differently).
    """

    is_on_demand = True  # only while a scanner uses it
    firmwares: ClassVar[Mapping[str, Sequence[Endpoint]]] = {}
    bluetooth: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset()  # firmwares that serve Bluetooth too (multiprotocol over CPC)

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return [Endpoint(USB_DRIVER, self.name, self.name, is_shared=True, instance=self)]

    async def identify(self, path: str) -> str | tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None:
        """The firmware the device at ``path`` runs, or None when it isn't one of its kind; with the serial settings it
        found the device at where they may differ from the firmware's, ``("deconz", {"baud": 38400})``: the device's
        endpoints take them."""
        return None

    def serves(self, firmware: str | None, path: str, params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[Endpoint]:
        """What ``firmware`` serves on the device at ``path``, ``params`` overriding its serial settings."""
        endpoints = self.firmwares.get(firmware or "", [])
        return [replace(e, url=e.url.format(device=path), params={**e.params, **(params or {})}) for e in endpoints]

    def flashable(self, path: str, channel: str) -> list[str]:
        """Firmwares the device at ``path`` can be switched to on the ``stable`` or ``dev`` channel."""
        return []

    async def flash(self, path: str, firmware: str, channel: str, cache: Path):
        raise NotImplementedError(f"{type(self).__name__} can't flash")


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/platform.py
================================================================================
"""The host every peripheral runs on, as its ``self.platform``: the facts it knows and its resources."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from contextlib import AbstractAsyncContextManager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.repository.memory import DeviceRepositoryMemory
from majordom_integration_sdk.repository.protocol import DeviceRepositoryProtocol
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.credentials import WifiCredentials

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral

type MakeDeviceRepository = Callable[[str], AbstractAsyncContextManager[DeviceRepositoryProtocol]]


def _in_memory() -> MakeDeviceRepository:
    store: dict[UUID, dict[str, Any]] = {}  # shared by the repositories of every peripheral
    return lambda key: DeviceRepositoryMemory(key, store).session()


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Platform:
    """The host every peripheral runs on, the same object for all of them as ``self.platform``: a controller is given
    it, ``peripherals(platform)``, and the runtime sets it on the others. It holds the facts the host knows as plain
    fields, and its resources, scoped to the peripheral passed::

        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repository:
            ...
        cache = self.platform.documents_folder(self) / "cache.json"

    Facts change only by replacement: the host builds a new platform (``dataclasses.replace``) and gives it to the
    runtime (`Runtime.update_platform`), which points every peripheral at it and tells the ones that run
    (``platform_facts_did_change``). Read ``self.platform`` when you need a fact: a platform kept holds the old ones.
    """

    # Where each peripheral gets a folder of its own, by its key: the Hub's, or a local one under the dev runner
    documents_root: Path
    # One unit of work on the device repository, scoped to the devices of the peripheral keyed; in memory by default
    make_device_repository: MakeDeviceRepository = field(default_factory=_in_memory)
    region: str | None = None  # RF region for sub-GHz radios, a Z-Wave JS name: "Europe", "USA", …
    wifi: WifiCredentials | None = None  # the network to provision Wi-Fi devices onto
    thread_dataset: str | None = None  # active operational dataset of the hub's Thread network, hex TLVs

    def documents_folder(self, peripheral: Peripheral) -> Path:
        """The folder of ``peripheral``, by its key, created on use: what it keeps across restarts that doesn't belong
        in the device database (certificates, protocol caches, a container's data)."""
        folder = self.documents_root / peripheral.key
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return folder

    def device_repository(self, peripheral: Peripheral) -> AbstractAsyncContextManager[DeviceRepositoryProtocol]:
        """One unit of work on the device repository, scoped to the devices of ``peripheral``, by its key: a
        controller's is its slug, the ``integration`` of every `Device` it keeps."""
        return self.make_device_repository(peripheral.key)

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/__init__.py
================================================================================
"""Device persistence for integrations — one protocol, two standalone implementations."""

from .memory import DeviceRepositoryMemory
from .protocol import DeviceRepositoryProtocol
from .sqlite import SqliteDeviceRepository

__all__ = ["DeviceRepositoryProtocol", "DeviceRepositoryMemory", "SqliteDeviceRepository"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/_record.py
================================================================================
"""Internal record helpers shared by the SDK's repository implementations.

A stored record is one JSON-safe dict per device holding *everything* known about it —
info, ``integration_data`` and ``parameters`` (from a :class:`DeviceState`). A ``Device``
lacks the parameters, and a ``DeviceState`` built without ``integration_data`` doesn't hold
the stored one; merging keeps both halves and lets a read deserialize into whichever view
(``as_``) the caller asks for.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState

type Record = dict[str, Any]


def dump(device: BaseModel, exclude: set[str] | None = None) -> Record:
    """JSON-safe dump, so records round-trip identically through memory or SQLite.

    Goes through ``model_dump_json`` rather than ``model_dump(mode="json")`` — the JSON
    serializer is the one these models are actually exercised against (``ParameterState``
    base64-encodes its ``bytes`` value there), so it's what the SQLite rows already store.
    """
    return json.loads(device.model_dump_json(exclude=exclude))


def merge(base: Record | None, device: Device | DeviceState) -> Record:
    """Merge a device into an existing record without clobbering the other view's fields: an unset
    ``integration_data`` (its default) only where the record has none (the ``{}`` or null the Hub stores a device with
    before pairing is none), so that filling the default in place counts."""
    unset = {"integration_data"} - device.model_fields_set if base and base.get("integration_data") else set()
    return {**(base or {}), **dump(device, exclude=unset)}


__all__ = ["Record", "dump", "merge"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/memory.py
================================================================================
"""In-memory :class:`DeviceRepositoryProtocol` implementation.

A legitimate, lightweight persistence choice for standalone/dev runs and tests — not a
mock. State lives in a dict for the process lifetime; use :class:`SqliteDeviceRepository`
when you need it to survive a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.repository._record import Record, dump, merge
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterState, ParameterVisibility


class DeviceRepositoryMemory:
    """Stores device records in a dict shared across sessions.

    Pass ``integration`` to scope every operation to that integration's devices (the guard
    the Hub sets when handing a repository to a controller). ``None`` gives full access.
    """

    def __init__(self, integration: str | None = None, store: dict[UUID, Record] | None = None):
        self.integration = integration
        self._store: dict[UUID, Record] = store if store is not None else {}

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def session(self) -> AsyncGenerator[DeviceRepositoryMemory]:
        """One unit of work: what ``Platform.make_device_repository`` returns for its integration."""
        yield self

    def _in_scope(self, record: Record) -> bool:
        return self.integration is None or record.get("integration") == self.integration

    def _owned(self, device_id: UUID) -> Record | None:
        record = self._store.get(device_id)
        return record if record is not None and self._in_scope(record) else None

    async def get_all[T: Device](self, as_: type[T] = Device) -> list[T]:
        return [as_.model_validate(r) for r in self._store.values() if self._in_scope(r)]

    async def get[T: Device](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = Device) -> T | None:
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def state[T: DeviceState](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = DeviceState) -> T | None:
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def get_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_id: UUID) -> ParameterState | None:
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        if not record:
            return None
        return next(
            (ParameterState.model_validate(p) for p in record.get("parameters", []) if p["id"] == str(parameter_id)),
            None,
        )

    async def save(self, device: Device | DeviceState, previous_id: UUID | None = None):
        if self.integration is not None and device.integration != self.integration:
            raise PermissionError(f"Device {device.id} is outside integration scope {self.integration!r}")
        base = self._store.pop(previous_id, None) if previous_id is not None and previous_id != device.id else None
        self._store[device.id] = merge(base if base is not None else self._store.get(device.id), device)

    async def save_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_state: ParameterState):
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        if not record:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown or out-of-scope device {device_id}")
        updated = dump(parameter_state)
        record["parameters"] = [
            updated if p["id"] == str(parameter_state.id) else p for p in record.get("parameters", [])
        ]

    # Hub-internal (not on DeviceRepositoryProtocol); still scope-checked.

    async def update_parameter_visibility(self, parameter_id: UUID, visibility: ParameterVisibility):
        for record in self._store.values():
            if not self._in_scope(record):
                continue
            for parameter in record.get("parameters", []):
                if parameter["id"] == str(parameter_id):
                    parameter["visibility"] = visibility.value
                    return

    async def delete(self, device_id: UUID):
        if self._owned(device_id):
            self._store.pop(device_id, None)


__all__ = ["DeviceRepositoryMemory"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/protocol.py
================================================================================
"""The device-repository interface a controller talks to.

A controller never touches a database directly — it goes through this protocol, obtained
from its platform's ``device_repository(self)`` (an async context manager scoping one unit of
work). The
Hub backs it with its shared SQLAlchemy database; the SDK ships two first-class
implementations for standalone/dev use — :class:`DeviceRepositoryMemory` and
:class:`SqliteDeviceRepository`.

**Integration scope.** The repository is bound to one integration at construction, so there
is no ``integration`` argument on the reads: an integration only ever sees its own devices.
Out-of-scope reads come back ``None``/empty and out-of-scope writes raise — a guard against
carelessness, not a security boundary. Constructing with ``integration=None`` gives full
access (the Hub's own higher-level use).

**Typed reads.** ``as_`` deserializes into your own ``Device[MyData]`` /
``DeviceState[MyData, MyParameterData]`` (or a subclass), so ``integration_data`` comes back
typed instead of a bare dict::

    async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
        device = await repo.get(device_id, as_=MyDevice)  # class MyDevice(Device[MyData])

**Not here on purpose:** ``delete`` and ``update_parameter_visibility`` are Hub-internal
lifecycle operations. They exist on the concrete implementations, but are kept off this
protocol so an integration can't reach past its scope.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterState


@runtime_checkable
class DeviceRepositoryProtocol(Protocol):
    """Persistence for one integration's paired devices and their parameter states."""

    async def get_all[T: Device](self, as_: type[T] = Device) -> list[T]:
        """Every paired device in scope, deserialized as ``as_``."""
        ...

    async def get[T: Device](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = Device) -> T | None:
        """The device (info + ``integration_data``) as ``as_``, or ``None`` if unknown/out of scope."""
        ...

    async def state[T: DeviceState](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = DeviceState) -> T | None:
        """The device with its parameter states as ``as_``, or ``None`` if unknown/out of scope."""
        ...

    async def get_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_id: UUID) -> ParameterState | None:
        """One parameter's current state, or ``None`` if the device/parameter is unknown/out of scope."""
        ...

    async def save(self, device: Device | DeviceState, previous_id: UUID | None = None):
        """Insert or update a device, merging into whatever is already stored.

        Saving a ``Device`` updates its info/``integration_data``; saving a ``DeviceState``
        updates its info/``parameters``, and its ``integration_data`` only when it was given
        one — neither clobbers the other's fields. ``previous_id``
        renames an existing record before the write (pairing turning a provisional discovery
        id into the device's final id), carrying its stored data over. Rejects a device
        outside the bound integration's scope.
        """
        ...

    async def save_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_state: ParameterState):
        """Update a single parameter's value/state on an existing in-scope device."""
        ...


__all__ = ["DeviceRepositoryProtocol"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/sqlite.py
================================================================================
"""File-backed :class:`DeviceRepositoryProtocol` on the standard-library ``sqlite3``.

No third-party dependency: each device is stored as one row of JSON (the record already
stores pythonic parameter values as JSON via Pydantic). Suitable
for a standalone integration that needs its paired devices to survive a restart; the Hub
uses its own SQLAlchemy-backed repository instead.

``sqlite3`` is synchronous; calls are cheap and local, so the async methods invoke it
directly. Obtain a session with :meth:`session` (opens a connection, commits on clean exit).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.repository._record import Record, dump, merge
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterState, ParameterVisibility


class SqliteDeviceRepository:
    """Persists device records as JSON rows in a SQLite file.

    Pass ``integration`` to scope every operation to that integration's devices (the guard
    the Hub sets when handing a repository to a controller). ``None`` gives full access.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, integration: str | None = None):
        self.path = str(path)
        self.integration = integration
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices ("
                "  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, uuid TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,"
                "  integration TEXT NOT NULL, data TEXT NOT NULL)"
            )
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        return conn

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def session(self) -> AsyncGenerator[SqliteDeviceRepository]:
        """One unit of work: what ``Platform.make_device_repository`` returns for its integration."""
        # A fresh connection per unit of work; sharing one across concurrent tasks is unsafe.
        self._conn = self._connect()
        try:
            yield self
            self._conn.commit()
        finally:
            self._conn.close()
            del self._conn

    def _cursor(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = getattr(self, "_conn", None)
        if conn is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Use `async with repo.session():` before calling repository methods")
        return conn

    def _record(self, device_id: UUID) -> Record | None:
        """The stored record for an in-scope device, or None."""
        if self.integration is None:
            row = self._cursor().execute("SELECT data FROM devices WHERE uuid = ?", (str(device_id),)).fetchone()
        else:
            row = (
                self._cursor()
                .execute(
                    "SELECT data FROM devices WHERE uuid = ? AND integration = ?",
                    (str(device_id), self.integration),
                )
                .fetchone()
            )
        return json.loads(row["data"]) if row else None

    def _write(self, record: Record):
        self._cursor().execute(
            "INSERT INTO devices (uuid, integration, data) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(uuid) DO UPDATE SET integration = excluded.integration, data = excluded.data",
            (record["id"], record["integration"], json.dumps(record)),
        )

    async def get_all[T: Device](self, as_: type[T] = Device) -> list[T]:
        if self.integration is None:
            rows = self._cursor().execute("SELECT data FROM devices").fetchall()
        else:
            rows = (
                self._cursor().execute("SELECT data FROM devices WHERE integration = ?", (self.integration,)).fetchall()
            )
        return [as_.model_validate(json.loads(row["data"])) for row in rows]

    async def get[T: Device](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = Device) -> T | None:
        record = self._record(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def state[T: DeviceState](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = DeviceState) -> T | None:
        record = self._record(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def get_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_id: UUID) -> ParameterState | None:
        record = self._record(device_id)
        if not record:
            return None
        return next(
            (ParameterState.model_validate(p) for p in record.get("parameters", []) if p["id"] == str(parameter_id)),
            None,
        )

    async def save(self, device: Device | DeviceState, previous_id: UUID | None = None):
        if self.integration is not None and device.integration != self.integration:
            raise PermissionError(f"Device {device.id} is outside integration scope {self.integration!r}")
        base: Record | None = None
        if previous_id is not None and previous_id != device.id:
            base = self._record(previous_id)
            self._cursor().execute("DELETE FROM devices WHERE uuid = ?", (str(previous_id),))
        self._write(merge(base if base is not None else self._record(device.id), device))

    async def save_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_state: ParameterState):
        record = self._record(device_id)
        if not record:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown or out-of-scope device {device_id}")
        updated = dump(parameter_state)
        record["parameters"] = [
            updated if p["id"] == str(parameter_state.id) else p for p in record.get("parameters", [])
        ]
        self._write(record)

    # Hub-internal (not on DeviceRepositoryProtocol); still scope-checked.

    async def update_parameter_visibility(self, parameter_id: UUID, visibility: ParameterVisibility):
        for device in await self.get_all():
            record = self._record(device.id)
            if not record:
                continue
            if any(p["id"] == str(parameter_id) for p in record.get("parameters", [])):
                for parameter in record["parameters"]:
                    if parameter["id"] == str(parameter_id):
                        parameter["visibility"] = visibility.value
                self._write(record)
                return

    async def delete(self, device_id: UUID):
        if self._record(device_id) is None:
            return
        self._cursor().execute("DELETE FROM devices WHERE uuid = ?", (str(device_id),))


__all__ = ["SqliteDeviceRepository"]

================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/defaults.py
================================================================================
"""What a runtime runs by default, given explicitly: the defaults keep a composition root short and replaceable. Each
call builds new ones, so no two runtimes share a peripheral.

Under the Hub, hardware first (the order given is the order of preference)::

    Runtime(data, [Pinned(*mine), FixedPeripherals(*soldered), *default_peripherals(), *integrations], platform=...)

In library mode, one integration with what it needs::

    Runtime(data, [*default_peripherals(), HueController(platform)], platform=platform)
    Runtime(data, [HostNetwork(), ZeroconfDiscoveryService(), HueController(platform)], platform=platform)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import functools
import logging

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.host import BluetoothAdapters, HostNetwork
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.usb import UsbScanner
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.router import BLEService
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ssdp import SSDPDiscoveryService
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.builtin import otbr, silabs_multiprotocol
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose import Compose

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def default_peripherals(*, listen_address: str = "127.0.0.1") -> list[Peripheral]:
    """Everything the SDK runs around integrations, in the order it binds: the sticks plugged in (by
    `default_usb_drivers`) before the containers that serve over them, Docker Compose that runs those, the
    multiprotocol border router before the standalone one, the Bluetooth router before the integrations, so it takes
    every adapter. On-demand ones run only while used. The containers on the host network answer on
    ``listen_address`` (`Compose`): the hub only by default."""
    zeroconf = _zeroconf()
    return [
        UsbScanner(),
        BluetoothAdapters(),
        HostNetwork(),
        Compose(listen_address),
        silabs_multiprotocol(),
        otbr(),
        BLEService(),
        *([zeroconf()] if zeroconf else []),
        SSDPDiscoveryService(),
    ]


@functools.cache  # said once
def _zeroconf() -> type[Peripheral] | None:
    try:
        from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.zeroconf import ZeroconfDiscoveryService
    except ImportError:
        log.warning('No DNS-SD without zeroconf: pip install "majordom-integration-sdk[discovery]"')
        return None
    return ZeroconfDiscoveryService


__all__ = ["default_peripherals"]

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/output.py

"""The one ``output`` every peripheral of a runtime shares."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.controller.output import ControllerOutput, IntegrationError
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Discovery
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.event import Event
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.notification import Notification

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.controller.abstract_controller import AbstractController
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.runtime import Runtime


class HostOutput(ControllerOutput):
    """What every peripheral of a runtime tells, as its ``output``: its lifecycle goes to the runtime, a controller's
    reports to ``controller_output`` (the Hub). A controller that can't go on (an error not ``is_still_running``)
    fails in the runtime too, and one that changed what it provides has the runtime read it again."""

    def __init__(self, runtime: Runtime, controller_output: ControllerOutput):
        self.runtime, self.controller_output = runtime, controller_output

    # PeripheralOutput

    async def peripheral_did_change_provided(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_change_provided(peripheral)

    async def peripheral_did_learn(self, peripheral: Peripheral, facts: Mapping[str, Any]):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_learn(peripheral, facts)

    async def peripheral_did_stop(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_stop(peripheral)

    async def peripheral_did_fail(self, peripheral: Peripheral, reason: str):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_fail(peripheral, reason)

    # ControllerOutput

    async def controller_did_receive_discovery(self, controller: AbstractController, discovery: Discovery):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_receive_discovery(controller, discovery)

    async def controller_did_update_discovery(self, controller: AbstractController, discovery: Discovery):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_update_discovery(controller, discovery)

    async def controller_did_lose_discovery(self, controller: AbstractController, discovery_id: UUID):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_lose_discovery(controller, discovery_id)

    async def controller_did_connect_device(self, controller: AbstractController, device_id: UUID):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_connect_device(controller, device_id)

    async def controller_did_lose_device(self, controller: AbstractController, device_id: UUID):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_lose_device(controller, device_id)

    async def controller_did_receive_events(self, controller: AbstractController, events: Iterable[Event]):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_receive_events(controller, events)

    async def controller_did_encounter_error(self, controller: AbstractController, error: IntegrationError):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_encounter_error(controller, error)
        if not error.is_still_running:
            await self.runtime.peripheral_did_fail(controller, error.message)

    async def controller_did_resolve_error(self, controller: AbstractController, error_id: str):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_resolve_error(controller, error_id)

    async def controller_did_emit_notification(self, controller: AbstractController, notification: Notification):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_emit_notification(controller, notification)

    async def controller_did_change_provided(self, controller: AbstractController):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_change_provided(controller)
