"""How a settings model marks its fields for the host."""

from enum import StrEnum


class SettingsExtraField(StrEnum):
    """The JSON schema keywords a settings field is marked with: ``Field(json_schema_extra={Extra.read_only: True})``
    with ``from majordom_integration_sdk import SettingsExtraField as Extra``."""

    read_only = "readOnly"  # the peripheral fills it in itself; never the user, never kept
    write_only = "writeOnly"  # the user sets it, nothing reads it back: a secret


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/spec_drift.py
================================================================================
"""Source-agnostic spec-drift diffing — the shared engine behind the MVD canary and the zha /
matter-HA harvest refreshers.

A "spec" here is any ``dict`` keyed by an identity (e.g. ``(cluster_id, attribute_id)``) whose
values are the harvested judgment. :func:`diff_specs` compares a freshly-produced spec against the
committed baseline and tiers every change by risk, mirroring how Dependabot tiers a version bump:

    ADD          a key that didn't exist          — low risk (reveals a previously-uncurated item)
    REMOVE       a key that disappeared            — medium (something we surfaced may vanish)
    RECLASSIFY   an existing key's value changed   — HIGH (changes what current users already see)

CI runs the harvester, calls :func:`diff_specs` against the vendored artifact, and opens a
Dependabot-style PR when anything changed — highlighting RECLASSIFY at the top for human review.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Hashable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any


# Generic over the key type — `Mapping` is invariant in its key, so a plain
# `Mapping[Hashable, Any]` would reject perfectly valid concrete specs like
# `dict[tuple[int, int], str]`.
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DriftReport[K: Hashable]:
    added: dict[K, Any]
    removed: dict[K, Any]
    reclassified: dict[K, tuple[Any, Any]]  # key -> (old, new)

    @property
    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return not (self.added or self.removed or self.reclassified)

    @property
    def has_high_risk(self) -> bool:
        """RECLASSIFY changes an existing item's judgment — the only tier that can silently alter
        what current users already see, so it always warrants human review."""
        return bool(self.reclassified)

    def render(self, *, source: str = "spec", key_label: Callable[[K], str] | None = None) -> str:
        """Render a human-readable drift summary.

        ``key_label`` optionally resolves a key to a human name (e.g. a raw ``(cluster_id,
        attribute_id)`` -> ``"Chime.SelectedChime"``) so a reviewer reading the PR body sees what
        actually changed, not just numeric ids. It's kept out of the engine because the mapping is
        integration-specific (chip bindings for matter, zigpy for zha); each canary passes its own.
        A resolver that raises or returns falsy for a key falls back to the bare id.
        """

        def tag(key: K) -> str:
            label = None
            if key_label is not None:
                try:
                    label = key_label(key)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a name lookup must never break the drift report
                    label = None
            return f"{label}  {key!r}" if label else f"{key!r}"

        if self.is_empty:
            return f"[{source}] no drift"
        lines = [
            f"[{source}] drift: +{len(self.added)} added  -{len(self.removed)} removed  "
            f"~{len(self.reclassified)} reclassified"
        ]
        # RECLASSIFY first — it's the high-risk tier.
        for key, (old, new) in sorted(self.reclassified.items(), key=lambda kv: repr(kv[0])):
            lines.append(f"  ~ RECLASSIFY {tag(key)}: {old!r} -> {new!r}")
        for key, val in sorted(self.added.items(), key=lambda kv: repr(kv[0])):
            lines.append(f"  + ADD        {tag(key)}: {val!r}")
        for key, val in sorted(self.removed.items(), key=lambda kv: repr(kv[0])):
            lines.append(f"  - REMOVE     {tag(key)}: {val!r}")
        return "\n".join(lines)


def diff_specs[K: Hashable](current: Mapping[K, Any], baseline: Mapping[K, Any]) -> DriftReport[K]:
    """Diff a freshly-harvested ``current`` spec against the committed ``baseline``."""
    added = {k: current[k] for k in current if k not in baseline}
    removed = {k: baseline[k] for k in baseline if k not in current}
    reclassified = {k: (baseline[k], current[k]) for k in current if k in baseline and current[k] != baseline[k]}
    return DriftReport(added=added, removed=removed, reclassified=reclassified)


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/testing/__init__.py
================================================================================
"""Shared test doubles for integration test suites.

Both the Hub's own integration tests and third-party ``integration-*`` packages import these
instead of reinventing them, so every integration is exercised through the same harness:

- :class:`RecordingControllerOutput` — a spy implementing every ``ControllerOutput``
  callback, capturing what a controller reports back to the Hub: set it as its ``output``.
- :class:`FakePeripheral` — a peripheral that records how it is run: what it needs and provides (endpoints
  and the peripherals it brings along) is set per test, its starts can fail, its hooks answer as told.
- :class:`RecordingPeripheralOutput` — what any other peripheral tells the runtime, as its ``output``;
  :class:`RecordingRuntimeOutput` — what the runtime reports to the Hub.
- :class:`FakeCompose` — the container host without Docker, for the services an integration provides.
- Offline doubles of every capability (no radios/sockets touched): :class:`FakeBLESource` for the
  Bluetooth router to hear through (``router.add_source(source)``), :class:`FakeBLERouter`,
  :class:`FakeZeroconf` (the ``discovery`` extra) and :class:`FakeSSDP`. Each provides itself as
  ``.endpoint``, to bind as the controller's peripherals: ``Peripherals({"ble": router.endpoint})``.
- :func:`build_test_platform` — assembles a ``Platform`` with an in-memory device repository
  (its ``store`` yours to read), temp-dir storage and the facts you give, so a test can drive a
  controller (or any peripheral) exactly as the Hub would.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import functools
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel

from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities.ble import BLEConnection, BLEDiscoveryListener, BLEMatcher, OnAdvertisement
from majordom_integration_sdk.controller.output import ControllerOutput, IntegrationError
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Endpoint, Need, NoSettings, Peripheral, PeripheralChange, Service
from majordom_integration_sdk.platform import Platform
from majordom_integration_sdk.repository.memory import DeviceRepositoryMemory
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.router import BLEService
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ssdp import SSDPDiscoveryService
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose import Compose
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.credentials import WifiCredentials
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Discovery
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.event import Event
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.notification import Notification

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.controller.abstract_controller import AbstractController as _Controller
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import PeripheralStatus


class RecordingControllerOutput(ControllerOutput):
    """Captures every callback a controller makes, for assertions in tests."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.received_discoveries: list[Discovery] = []
        self.updated_discoveries: list[Discovery] = []
        self.lost_discoveries: list[UUID] = []
        self.connected_devices: list[UUID] = []
        self.lost_devices: list[UUID] = []
        self.events: list[Event] = []
        self.errors: dict[str, IntegrationError] = {}  # the active ones, by id
        self.error_log: list[IntegrationError | str] = []  # every report, and the id of every resolve
        self.notifications: list[Notification] = []
        self.provided_changes: list[_Controller] = []  # every time one said what it provides changed

    async def controller_did_receive_discovery(self, controller: _Controller, discovery: Discovery):
        self.received_discoveries.append(discovery)

    async def controller_did_update_discovery(self, controller: _Controller, discovery: Discovery):
        self.updated_discoveries.append(discovery)

    async def controller_did_lose_discovery(self, controller: _Controller, discovery_id: UUID):
        self.lost_discoveries.append(discovery_id)

    async def controller_did_connect_device(self, controller: _Controller, device_id: UUID):
        self.connected_devices.append(device_id)

    async def controller_did_lose_device(self, controller: _Controller, device_id: UUID):
        self.lost_devices.append(device_id)

    async def controller_did_receive_events(self, controller: _Controller, events: Iterable[Event]):
        self.events.extend(events)

    async def controller_did_encounter_error(self, controller: _Controller, error: IntegrationError):
        self.errors[error.id] = error
        self.error_log.append(error)

    async def controller_did_resolve_error(self, controller: _Controller, error_id: str):
        self.errors.pop(error_id, None)
        self.error_log.append(error_id)

    async def controller_did_emit_notification(self, controller: _Controller, notification: Notification):
        self.notifications.append(notification)

    async def controller_did_change_provided(self, controller: _Controller):
        self.provided_changes.append(controller)


class FakePeripheral(Peripheral):
    """A peripheral that records how it is run (``calls``: "start", "stop") and the changes it hears. Its first
    ``failures`` starts raise; ``answer`` is what its hooks return, or an exception they raise. Change ``provided``,
    then tell ``output``, as a real one does when a stick is plugged in."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        needs: Sequence[Need] = (),
        provides: Sequence[Endpoint | Peripheral] = (),
        *,
        is_on_demand: bool = False,
        failures: int = 0,
        answer: bool | Exception = False,
        settings: type[BaseModel] = NoSettings,
    ):
        self.name, self.needs, self.provided = name, list(needs), list(provides)
        self.is_on_demand = is_on_demand
        self.failures, self.answer = failures, answer
        self.settings_model = settings
        self.calls: list[str] = []
        self.changes: list[PeripheralChange | tuple[str, Any]] = []  # needs moved; ("settings"|"platform", before)

    @property
    def Settings(self) -> type[BaseModel]:
        return self.settings_model

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint | Peripheral]:
        return self.provided

    async def start(self):
        self.calls.append("start")
        if self.failures:
            self.failures -= 1
            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.name} broke")

    async def stop(self):
        self.calls.append("stop")

    async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change: PeripheralChange) -> bool:
        self.changes.append(change)
        return self._answer()

    async def settings_did_change(self, before: Any) -> bool:
        self.changes.append(("settings", before))
        return self._answer()

    async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before: Any) -> bool:
        self.changes.append(("platform", before))
        return self._answer()

    def _answer(self) -> bool:
        if isinstance(self.answer, Exception):
            raise self.answer
        return self.answer

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"FakePeripheral({self.name!r})"


class RecordingPeripheralOutput:
    """Captures what peripherals report to whatever runs them: set it as a peripheral's ``output``."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.changed: list[Peripheral] = []
        self.learned: list[tuple[Peripheral, Mapping[str, Any]]] = []
        self.stopped: list[Peripheral] = []
        self.failed: list[tuple[Peripheral, str]] = []

    async def peripheral_did_change_provided(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        self.changed.append(peripheral)

    async def peripheral_did_learn(self, peripheral: Peripheral, facts: Mapping[str, Any]):
        self.learned.append((peripheral, facts))

    async def peripheral_did_stop(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        self.stopped.append(peripheral)

    async def peripheral_did_fail(self, peripheral: Peripheral, reason: str):
        self.failed.append((peripheral, reason))


class RecordingRuntimeOutput:
    """Captures what a runtime reports to the Hub: every status in order, the last one by key, what was learned, the
    ones gone."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.statuses: list[tuple[str, PeripheralStatus]] = []
        self.learned: list[tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any]]] = []
        self.disappeared: list[Peripheral] = []

    def peripheral_did_change_status(self, peripheral: Peripheral, status: PeripheralStatus):
        self.statuses.append((peripheral.key, status))

    def peripheral_did_learn(self, peripheral: Peripheral, facts: Mapping[str, Any]):
        self.learned.append((peripheral.key, facts))

    def peripheral_did_disappear(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        self.disappeared.append(peripheral)

    def last(self, key: str) -> PeripheralStatus | None:
        return next((status for k, status in reversed(self.statuses) if k == key), None)


class FakeCompose(Compose):
    """Docker Compose without Docker: it renders, keeps ports and writes ``compose.json`` as the real one, and a
    container runs and answers once applied. ``calls`` are the docker commands it would have run."""

    def __init__(self, listen_address: str = "127.0.0.1"):
        super().__init__(listen_address)
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, ...]] = []

    async def _docker(self, *args: str) -> str:
        self.calls.append(args)
        return "\n".join(self._running) if "ps" in args else ""

    async def _is_up(self, service: Service) -> bool:
        return service.name in self._running


class FakeSSDP(SSDPDiscoveryService):
    """Real registration bookkeeping, but ``start``/``stop`` touch no network."""

    async def start(self):
        pass

    async def stop(self):
        pass


class FakeBLERouter(BLEService):
    """A router with no radio unless given `FakeBLESource`s; ``start``/``stop`` run no background tasks."""

    @property
    def registrations(self) -> list[tuple[BLEDiscoveryListener, list[BLEMatcher]]]:
        """Every listener registered (and not cancelled) with what it listens for, as a copy."""
        return [(listener, list(matchers)) for listener, matchers in self._listeners]

    async def start(self):
        await self._follow_bound()
        self._is_running = True
        await self._start_sources()

    async def stop(self):
        self._is_running = False
        await self._stop_sources()


def __getattr__(name: str):
    if name == "FakeZeroconf":  # the discovery extra (zeroconf): only for the suites that use it
        from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.zeroconf import ZeroconfDiscoveryService

        class FakeZeroconf(ZeroconfDiscoveryService):
            """Real registration bookkeeping, but ``start``/``stop`` touch no network."""

            async def start(self):
                pass

            async def stop(self):
                pass

        globals()[name] = FakeZeroconf
        return FakeZeroconf
    raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")


class FakeBLESource:
    """A Bluetooth radio for tests: ``advertise`` feeds the service it serves, ``connect`` returns
    ``connection`` (or fails when there is none). Use with ``BLEService(sources=[...])``."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str = "fake",
        connection: BLEConnection | None = None,
        is_pairable: bool = False,
        free_slots: int | None = None,
        is_loss_reported: bool = False,
    ):
        self.name = name
        self.connection = connection
        self.is_pairable = is_pairable
        self.free_slots = free_slots
        self.is_loss_reported = is_loss_reported
        self.on_advertisement: OnAdvertisement | None = None
        self.connected: list[str] = []

    async def start(self, on_advertisement: OnAdvertisement):
        self.on_advertisement = on_advertisement

    async def stop(self):
        self.on_advertisement = None

    async def connect(self, address: str, on_disconnect: Callable[[], None]) -> BLEConnection:
        if self.connection is None:
            raise ConnectionError(f"{self.name} can't reach {address}")
        self.connected.append(address)
        return self.connection

    def advertise(
        self,
        address: str,
        rssi: int = -60,
        local_name: str | None = None,
        service_uuids: list[str] | None = None,
        service_data: dict[str, bytes] | None = None,
        manufacturer_data: dict[int, bytes] | None = None,
    ):
        from bleak.backends.device import BLEDevice  # the ble extra
        from bleak.backends.scanner import AdvertisementData

        assert self.on_advertisement, f"{self.name} isn't listening"
        adv = AdvertisementData(
            local_name, manufacturer_data or {}, service_data or {}, service_uuids or [], None, rssi, ()
        )
        self.on_advertisement(BLEDevice(address, local_name, self.name), adv)  # details: the radio


def build_test_platform(
    documents_root: Path | None = None,
    *,
    region: str | None = None,
    wifi: WifiCredentials | None = None,
    thread_dataset: str | None = None,
    store: dict[UUID, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> Platform:
    """Assemble a ``Platform`` wired entirely with offline test doubles, as the Hub gives it to every peripheral: an
    in-memory repository each controller sees only its own devices of, scoped by its key, and the facts given.

    Pass ``documents_root`` as the root of the peripherals' folders; a fresh temp folder otherwise, removed when the
    process ends. Pass ``store`` to see every device kept there: ``DeviceRepositoryMemory(store=store)``.
    """
    store = store if store is not None else {}
    return Platform(
        documents_root=documents_root or Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=_temp_root().name)),
        make_device_repository=lambda key: DeviceRepositoryMemory(key, store).session(),
        region=region,
        wifi=wifi,
        thread_dataset=thread_dataset,
    )


@functools.cache
def _temp_root() -> tempfile.TemporaryDirectory[str]:
    """Where the platforms built without a root keep their folders, one each: removed when the process ends."""
    return tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="majordom-sdk-test-")


__all__ = [
    "RecordingControllerOutput",
    "FakePeripheral",

    "FakeBLESource",
    "FakeBLERouter",
    "FakeZeroconf",
    "FakeSSDP",
    "FakeCompose",
    "build_test_platform",
]

# schemas/ and the providers (BLE, DNS-SD, SSDP) are lifted verbatim from the Hub, which type-checks them under

# rules for just those paths — all SDK-native code stays fully checked. Re-home in the Hub.

    "majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/peripherals/providers/**",

invalid-assignment = "ignore"
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"

# The repository's typed reads use the `as_: type[T] = Device` idiom (same as the Hub's own
# repository) so callers get `get(id, as_=MyDevice) -> MyDevice` while the bare `get(id)`
# still returns a Device. ty rejects a concrete default for a TypeVar-typed parameter; the
# alternative is @overload on every read across the protocol and both implementations.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["majordom_integration_sdk/repository/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-parameter-default = "ignore"

# The runtime's tests stand plain objects in for bleak's (a BleakClient): ty can't match them
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/runtime/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

================================================================================
# FILE: tests/factories.py
================================================================================
"""Factories for the SDK's own test suite: tests import them, as ``tests/runtime`` has a conftest of its own."""

from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import (
    ParameterDataType,
    ParameterRole,
    ParameterState,
    ParameterVisibility,
)


def make_parameter_state(
    *,
    id: UUID | None = None,
    name: str = "Power",
    data_type: ParameterDataType = ParameterDataType.bool,
    role: ParameterRole = ParameterRole.control,
    visibility: ParameterVisibility = ParameterVisibility.user,
) -> ParameterState:
    state = ParameterState(
        id=id or uuid4(),
        name=name,
        data_type=data_type,
        role=role,
        visibility=visibility,
        integration_data=None,
    )
    if data_type is ParameterDataType.bool:
        state.value = True
    return state


def make_device_state(
    *,
    id: UUID | None = None,
    integration: str = "example",
    name: str = "Lamp",
    parameters: list[ParameterState] | None = None,
) -> DeviceState:
    return DeviceState(
        id=id or uuid4(),
        name=name,
        room_id=uuid4(),
        transport="wifi",
        integration=integration,
        manufacturer="ACME",
        parameters=parameters if parameters is not None else [make_parameter_state()],
    )

# FILE: tests/runtime/conftest.py

import pytest
from support import STARTED

from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import runtime as module
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services import builtin, compose


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def quick_retries(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "RETRY_DELAYS", (0.01, 0.01, 0.01))
    monkeypatch.setattr(compose, "READY_POLL", 0.01)
    monkeypatch.setattr(builtin, "POLL", 0.01)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
async def stopped():
    yield
    while STARTED:
        await STARTED.pop().stop()


================================================================================
# FILE: tests/runtime/support.py
================================================================================
"""Driving a runtime in tests: run it, wait for what it started, tell it what changed."""

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path

from majordom_integration_sdk import Peripheral
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import PeripheralState, Runtime
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import build_test_platform


async def settle(runtime: Runtime):
    """Let every start in flight finish, and the runtime act on it."""
    while pending := [task for task in runtime._tasks if not task.done()]:
        await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)


async def until(runtime: Runtime, condition: Callable[[], bool], timeout: float = 2, settled: bool = True):
    """Wait for what a timer does, e.g. a retry; then, if ``settled``, for what it set off."""
    async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):
        while not condition():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.005)
    if settled:
        await settle(runtime)


STARTED: list[Runtime] = []  # stopped after each test


async def run(path: Path, *peripherals: Peripheral, settled: bool = True, **kwargs) -> Runtime:
    """A runtime of ``peripherals``, started; with ``settled``, once every start it set off returned. Its platform
    keeps the documents under ``data/peripherals`` unless given."""
    kwargs.setdefault("platform", build_test_platform(path / "data" / "peripherals"))
    runtime = Runtime(path / "data", peripherals, **kwargs)
    STARTED.append(runtime)
    await runtime.start()
    if settled:
        await settle(runtime)
    return runtime


async def changed(runtime: Runtime, peripheral: Peripheral):
    """``peripheral`` changed what it provides or brings along on its own, and told the runtime."""
    await peripheral.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(peripheral)
    await settle(runtime)


def state(runtime: Runtime, peripheral: Peripheral) -> PeripheralState:
    return runtime.status(peripheral).state


================================================================================
# FILE: tests/runtime/test_binding.py
================================================================================
"""How the runtime binds needs: in the order it is given, single-use endpoints once, and why a need stays unbound."""

import json

import pytest
from support import run, settle

from majordom_integration_sdk import Endpoint, Need
from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import BLE_ROUTER
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import PeripheralState, PeripheralStatus
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import StatusKind as K
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakePeripheral

ADAPTERS = [Endpoint("ble", "bluez", "hci0"), Endpoint("ble", "bluez", "hci1")]
ROUTER = Endpoint("ble", "router", "router", is_shared=True, instance=object())


def adapters() -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("bluetooth-adapters", provides=ADAPTERS)


def router() -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral(
        "ble-router",
        [Need("ble", ["bluez"], is_many=True, is_required=False)],
        [ROUTER],
        is_on_demand=True,
        answer=True,
    )


async def test_a_many_need_binds_every_free_matching_endpoint(tmp_path):
    sniffer = FakePeripheral("sniffer", [Need("ble", ["bluez"], is_many=True)])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, adapters(), sniffer)

    assert runtime.bound(sniffer) == {"ble": ADAPTERS}
    assert sniffer.peripherals.endpoints("ble") == ADAPTERS
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="endpoints"):
        sniffer.peripherals.endpoint("ble")
    assert runtime.providers(sniffer) == {"ble": ["bluetooth-adapters", "bluetooth-adapters"]}  # one per endpoint


async def test_a_many_need_that_finds_nothing_is_unbound(tmp_path):
    sniffer = FakePeripheral("sniffer", [Need("lora", is_many=True)])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, sniffer)
    assert runtime.unbound(sniffer) == {"lora": "need lora/*: nothing offers it"}


async def test_an_in_process_provider_is_a_shared_endpoint_carrying_itself(tmp_path):
    ble, matter, homekit = router(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("ble", ["router"])]), None
    homekit = FakePeripheral("homekit", [Need("ble", ["router"])])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, ble, matter, homekit)

    instance = ROUTER.instance
    assert matter.peripherals.instance(BLE_ROUTER) is instance and homekit.peripherals.instance(BLE_ROUTER) is instance
    assert runtime.users(ble) == ["matter", "homekit"]


async def test_the_first_given_takes_every_adapter_and_the_others_hear_what_to_need(tmp_path):
    ble, raw = router(), FakePeripheral("raw", [Need("ble", ["bluez"])])
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("ble", ["router"])])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, adapters(), ble, raw, matter)

    assert ble.peripherals.endpoints("ble") == ADAPTERS
    assert runtime.status(matter).state == PeripheralState.RUNNING  # the others run on
    assert runtime.unbound(raw) == {
        "ble": 'need ble/bluez: every provider taken by ble-router — use Need("ble", ["router"])'
    }


async def test_a_router_nothing_uses_leaves_the_adapters_to_who_needs_them_raw(tmp_path):
    ble, raw = router(), FakePeripheral("raw", [Need("ble", ["bluez"])])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, adapters(), ble, raw)

    assert runtime.status(ble) == PeripheralStatus(PeripheralState.WAITING, K.UNUSED, "nothing that runs uses it")
    assert runtime.status(raw).state == PeripheralState.RUNNING
    assert raw.peripherals.endpoint("ble") == ADAPTERS[0]


async def test_on_demand_peripherals_binding_only_each_other_dont_run(tmp_path):
    a = FakePeripheral("a", [Need("b", is_required=False)], [Endpoint("a", is_shared=True)], is_on_demand=True)
    b = FakePeripheral("b", [Need("a", is_required=False)], [Endpoint("b", is_shared=True)], is_on_demand=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, a, b)
    assert (
        runtime.status(a)
        == runtime.status(b)
        == PeripheralStatus(PeripheralState.WAITING, K.UNUSED, "nothing that runs uses it")
    )
    assert a.calls == b.calls == []


async def test_a_single_use_endpoint_goes_to_the_first_given_and_then_to_the_next(tmp_path):
    stick = FakePeripheral("stick", provides=[Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "/dev/ttyUSB0")])
    first, second = FakePeripheral("first", [Need("zigbee")]), FakePeripheral("second", [Need("zigbee")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, first, second)
    assert runtime.status(first).state == PeripheralState.RUNNING
    assert runtime.status(second) == PeripheralStatus(
        PeripheralState.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, "need zigbee/*: every provider taken by first"
    )

    await runtime.disable(first)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert runtime.status(second).state == PeripheralState.RUNNING


async def test_an_adapter_goes_by_the_order_given_alone(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    reserved = {"settings": {}, "reserved": {"matterjs-server": {"ble": "hci1"}}}  # kept by an older runtime
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps(reserved))
    ble = router()
    server = FakePeripheral("matterjs-server", [Need("ble", ["bluez"])], [Endpoint("matter", "x", "ws")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, adapters(), ble, FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("ble", ["router"])]), server)

    assert ble.peripherals.endpoints("ble") == ADAPTERS
    assert runtime.unbound(server) == {
        "ble": 'need ble/bluez: every provider taken by ble-router — use Need("ble", ["router"])'
    }
    assert "reserved" not in runtime.state and not hasattr(runtime, "reserve")


async def test_the_first_given_of_two_providers_serves_a_need(tmp_path):
    multipan = FakePeripheral("silabs-multiprotocol", provides=[Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest", "a", is_shared=True)])
    otbr = FakePeripheral("otbr", provides=[Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest", "b", is_shared=True)])
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, multipan, otbr, matter)
    assert runtime.providers(matter) == {"thread": "silabs-multiprotocol"}
    assert not hasattr(runtime, "pin")  # the order given and Pinned say what to prefer


async def test_a_provider_that_cant_run_says_why(tmp_path):
    multipan = FakePeripheral(
        "silabs-multiprotocol", [Need("multipan", ["silabs-cpc"])], [Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp")], is_on_demand=True
    )
    zigbee = FakePeripheral("zigbee", [Need("zigbee", ["ezsp", "znp"])])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, multipan, zigbee)
    assert runtime.unbound(zigbee) == {
        "zigbee": "need zigbee/ezsp|znp: silabs-multiprotocol can't run (need multipan/silabs-cpc: nothing offers it)"
    }
    assert runtime.unbound(multipan) == {"multipan": "need multipan/silabs-cpc: nothing offers it"}


async def test_a_need_one_that_doesnt_run_could_bind_has_no_reason(tmp_path):
    host = FakePeripheral("host", provides=[Endpoint("ip", is_shared=True)])
    server = FakePeripheral("server", [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("matter")], is_on_demand=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, host, server)
    assert runtime.unbound(server) == {}
    assert runtime.status(server).detail == "nothing that runs uses it"


async def test_what_a_firmware_would_serve_through_what_runs_here(tmp_path):
    multipan = FakePeripheral(
        "silabs-multiprotocol",
        [Need("multipan")],
        [Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp"), Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest")],
        is_on_demand=True,
    )
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, multipan, FakePeripheral("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")]))
    assert runtime.reach([Endpoint("multipan", "silabs-cpc")]) == ["zigbee"]  # thread: no one needs it
    assert runtime.reach([Endpoint("zwave")]) == []


================================================================================
# FILE: tests/runtime/test_ble_router.py
================================================================================
"""The Bluetooth router: what listeners hear from several radios, and which radio connects."""

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import Mock
from uuid import UUID

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import BLEBusyError, BLEConnection, BLEDiscoveryInfo, BLEMatcher
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Endpoint, Peripherals
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.router import BLEService
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakeBLERouter, FakeBLESource

MATTER = UUID("0000fff6-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb")
APPLE = 0x004C


class Listener:
    def __init__(self):
        self.found: list[BLEDiscoveryInfo] = []
        self.updated: list[BLEDiscoveryInfo] = []
        self.removed: list[BLEDiscoveryInfo] = []

    async def ble_did_discover_device(self, ble, info):
        self.found.append(info)

    async def ble_did_update_device(self, ble, info):
        self.updated.append(info)

    async def ble_did_remove_device(self, ble, info):
        self.removed.append(info)


async def settle():
    for _ in range(3):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)


@pytest.fixture
async def radios():
    near, far = (
        FakeBLESource("near", connection=Mock(spec=BLEConnection)),
        FakeBLESource("far", connection=Mock(spec=BLEConnection)),
    )
    ble = BLEService(sources=[near, far])
    await ble.start()
    yield ble, near, far
    await ble.stop()


async def test_listeners_of_the_same_service_all_hear_it(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    first, second = Listener(), Listener()
    ble.register(first, {MATTER})
    ble.register(second, {MATTER})

    near.advertise("AA", service_data={str(MATTER): b"\x00"})
    await settle()
    assert len(first.found) == len(second.found) == 1


async def test_matchers_select_by_manufacturer_data_and_name(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    homekit, named = Listener(), Listener()
    ble.register(homekit, [BLEMatcher(manufacturer_id=APPLE, manufacturer_data_start=b"\x06")])
    ble.register(named, [BLEMatcher(local_name_prefix="Improv")])

    near.advertise("AA", manufacturer_data={APPLE: b"\x10\x05"})  # an iPhone nearby
    near.advertise("BB", manufacturer_data={APPLE: b"\x06\x31"}, local_name="Improv-1")
    await settle()
    assert [i.device.address for i in homekit.found] == ["BB"]
    assert [i.device.address for i in named.found] == ["BB"]


async def test_a_device_heard_by_two_radios_is_one_device_seen_by_the_stronger(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    listener = Listener()
    ble.register(listener, {MATTER})

    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90, service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50, service_uuids=[str(MATTER)], local_name="Bulb")
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90, service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])  # no scan response: no name
    await settle()
    assert len(listener.found) == 1
    assert [i.source for i in listener.updated] == ["near"]
    assert ble.devices()[0].advertisement.local_name == "Bulb"


async def test_a_device_is_removed_once_no_radio_hears_it(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    listener = Listener()
    ble.register(listener, {MATTER})
    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    await settle()

    ble._removal_grace_sec = 0
    await ble.perform_scan()
    assert [i.device.address for i in listener.removed] == ["AA"]
    assert ble.devices() == []


async def test_a_device_whose_radio_is_leased_stays_until_the_lease_ends(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    listener = Listener()
    ble.register(listener, {MATTER})
    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    await settle()
    ble._removal_grace_sec = 0

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="esphome"):  # its radio silenced while the user presses the button
        await ble.perform_scan()
        assert listener.removed == [] and len(ble.devices()) == 1
    await ble.perform_scan()
    assert [i.device.address for i in listener.removed] == ["AA"]


async def test_cancelled_listeners_hear_nothing(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    listener = Listener()
    cancel = ble.register(listener, {MATTER})
    cancel()
    cancel()

    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    await settle()
    assert listener.found == []


async def test_connects_through_the_stronger_radio_and_falls_back(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90)
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50)
    await settle()

    assert await ble.connect("AA") is near.connection
    near.connection = None
    assert await ble.connect("AA") is far.connection
    far.connection = None
    with pytest.raises(ConnectionError, match="near.*far"):
        await ble.connect("AA")


async def test_a_lease_takes_the_radio_hearing_the_device_best(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90)
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter") as lease:
        assert lease.source == "near"
        assert await lease.connect() is near.connection
        assert (near.connected, far.connected) == (["AA"], [])


async def test_a_lease_stops_only_its_radio_scanning_until_released(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    near.advertise("AA")
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        assert near.on_advertisement is None
        assert far.on_advertisement is not None
        await ble.scan_actively(0)
        await ble._revive_silent()
        await ble.add_source(proxy := FakeBLESource("proxy"))
        assert near.on_advertisement is None
        assert proxy.on_advertisement is not None
    assert near.on_advertisement is not None


class PausableFakeBLESource(FakeBLESource):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.calls: list[str] = []

    async def start(self, on_advertisement):
        self.calls.append("start")
        await super().start(on_advertisement)

    async def stop(self):
        self.calls.append("stop")
        await super().stop()

    async def pause_scanning(self):
        self.calls.append("pause")

    async def resume_scanning(self):
        self.calls.append("resume")


async def test_a_lease_pauses_a_radio_that_can_pause_instead_of_stopping_it(radios):
    ble, _, _ = radios
    await ble.add_source(proxy := PausableFakeBLESource("proxy"))
    proxy.advertise("AA", rssi=-10)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter") as lease:
        assert lease.source == "proxy"
        assert proxy.calls == ["start", "resume", "pause"]
    assert proxy.calls == ["start", "resume", "pause", "resume"]


async def test_a_radio_that_can_pause_is_paused_exactly_while_leased_across_a_router_restart(radios):
    """A lease held across a restart keeps its radio subscribed (its connects go through it) and muted; one that ended
    while the router was stopped leaves it hearing once the router starts."""
    ble, _, _ = radios
    await ble.add_source(proxy := PausableFakeBLESource("proxy"))
    proxy.advertise("AA", rssi=-10)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        await ble.stop()
        await ble.start()
        assert proxy.on_advertisement is not None and proxy.calls[-1] == "pause"
    assert proxy.calls[-1] == "resume"

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        await ble.stop()
    await ble.start()
    assert proxy.on_advertisement is not None and proxy.calls[-1] == "resume"


async def test_a_radio_that_can_pause_added_while_leased_is_started_paused(radios):
    ble, _, _ = radios
    await ble.add_source(proxy := PausableFakeBLESource("proxy"))
    proxy.advertise("AA", rssi=-10)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        await ble.add_source(again := PausableFakeBLESource("proxy"))  # its node reconnected: another source
        assert again.calls == ["start", "pause"]  # subscribed for the lease's connects, and muted
    assert again.calls == ["start", "pause", "resume"] and again.on_advertisement is not None


async def test_a_second_lease_waits_then_takes_the_next_radio(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90)
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        started = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
        async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", wait=0.05) as lease:
            assert lease.source == "far"
            assert asyncio.get_running_loop().time() - started >= 0.05


async def test_a_connect_skips_leased_radios_and_fails_when_all_are(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90)
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        assert await ble.connect("AA") is far.connection
        async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", wait=0):
            with pytest.raises(BLEBusyError):
                await ble.connect("AA")


async def test_a_lease_cycles_through_busy_radios_until_it_gives_up(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90)
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50)
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"), ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter", wait=0):
        started = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
        with pytest.raises(BLEBusyError, match="hear AA are busy"):
            async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", timeout=0.1, wait=0.02):
                pass
        assert asyncio.get_running_loop().time() - started >= 0.1


async def test_a_lease_freed_meanwhile_is_taken_on_the_next_round(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50)
    await settle()

    held = asyncio.Event()

    async def hold():
        async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
            held.set()
            await asyncio.sleep(0.03)

    task = asyncio.create_task(hold())
    await held.wait()
    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", wait=0.01) as lease:  # only near hears it
        assert lease.source == "near"
    await task


async def test_a_cancelled_lease_releases_its_radio(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    near.advertise("AA")
    await settle()
    held = asyncio.Event()

    async def hold():
        async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
            held.set()
            await asyncio.Event().wait()

    task = asyncio.create_task(hold())
    await held.wait()
    task.cancel()
    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
        await task
    assert near.on_advertisement is not None
    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", wait=0) as lease:
        assert lease.source == "near"


async def test_a_lease_cancelled_while_waiting_holds_nothing(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    near.advertise("AA")
    await settle()

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="matter"):
        waiting = asyncio.create_task(ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", wait=1).__aenter__())
        await settle()
        waiting.cancel()
        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
            await waiting
    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="improv", wait=0) as lease:
        assert lease.source == "near"
    assert near.on_advertisement and far.on_advertisement


async def test_a_listener_registered_later_hears_devices_already_around(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    await settle()

    listener = Listener()
    ble.register(listener, {MATTER})
    await settle()
    assert [i.device.address for i in listener.found] == ["AA"]


def test_a_fake_router_shows_who_registered_for_what():
    router = FakeBLERouter()
    cancel = router.register(listener := Listener(), [MATTER])
    registered = [(listener, [BLEMatcher(service_uuid=MATTER)])]
    assert router.registrations == registered

    router.registrations.clear()  # a copy: reading it changes nothing
    assert router.registrations == registered
    cancel()
    assert router.registrations == []


async def test_a_radio_that_fails_to_stop_is_let_go_of_all_the_same(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios

    class Gone(FakeBLESource):
        async def stop(self):
            raise ConnectionError("its node went away")

    await ble.add_source(Gone("proxy"))
    await ble.remove_source("proxy")
    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    await settle()
    assert ble.devices()[0].source == "near" and "proxy" not in ble._candidates("AA")


async def test_a_stopped_router_lets_go_of_the_radios_it_was_bound_to():
    proxy, given = FakeBLESource("esphome:aa"), FakeBLESource("given")
    ble = BLEService(sources=[given])
    ble.peripherals = Peripherals({"ble": [Endpoint("ble", "esphome-proxy", "esphome:aa", instance=proxy)]})
    await ble.start()
    await ble.stop()
    assert list(ble._sources) == ["given"]  # the runtime binds them anew before its next start

    ble.peripherals = Peripherals({"ble": []})  # the node went meanwhile
    await ble.start()
    assert list(ble._sources) == ["given"] and proxy.on_advertisement is None
    await ble.stop()


async def test_a_silent_radio_is_restarted(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    near.on_advertisement = None  # bluetoothd restarted: the scanner is gone without a word
    far.advertise("AA")
    await settle()

    ble._silence_sec = 0.01
    await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
    far.advertise("AA")
    await ble._revive_silent()
    assert near.on_advertisement is not None  # listening again


async def test_a_silent_radio_whose_loss_is_reported_otherwise_is_never_restarted():
    proxy = FakeBLESource("esphome:aa", is_loss_reported=True)  # the node's API connection tells when it goes
    ble = BLEService(sources=[proxy])
    await ble.start()
    hearing = proxy.on_advertisement

    ble._silence_sec = 0.01
    await asyncio.sleep(0.02)  # no Bluetooth device around it
    await ble._revive_silent()
    assert proxy.on_advertisement is hearing  # still subscribed: a restart would drop the links it proxies
    await ble.stop()


async def test_a_local_adapter_stops_scanning_while_it_connects(monkeypatch):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    scanning = []

    class Scanner:
        def __init__(self, **kwargs):
            pass

        async def start(self):
            scanning.append(True)

        async def stop(self):
            scanning.append(False)

    class Client:
        def __init__(self, device, **kwargs):
            pass

        async def connect(self):
            assert scanning[-1] is False, "connecting while discovering: many adapters stall"

    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "BleakScanner", Scanner)
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "BleakClient", Client)
    adapter = LocalAdapter("hci0")
    await adapter.start(lambda device, adv: None)

    await adapter.connect("AA", lambda: None)
    assert scanning == [True, False, True]


def test_a_local_connection_reports_the_mtu_bluez_negotiated():
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import _BleakConnection

    # bleak reports BlueZ's MTU as 23 until it is acquired, while every characteristic already knows the real one
    characteristics = {1: SimpleNamespace(max_write_without_response_size=244)}
    client = SimpleNamespace(mtu_size=23, services=SimpleNamespace(characteristics=characteristics))

    assert _BleakConnection(client, "hci0").mtu == 247


async def test_a_device_is_seen_as_the_strongest_radio_hears_it(radios):
    ble, near, far = radios
    far.advertise("AA", rssi=-90, service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    near.advertise("AA", rssi=-50, service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    await settle()

    info = ble.devices()[0]
    assert (info.source, info.rssi) == ("near", -50)
    assert info.last_seen > 0
    assert info.device.details == "near"  # bleak's device as that radio has it


async def test_a_service_data_matcher_needs_the_data(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    listener = Listener()
    ble.register(listener, [BLEMatcher(service_data_uuid=MATTER)])

    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])  # only listed: no data to read
    near.advertise("BB", service_data={str(MATTER): b"\x00"})
    await settle()
    assert [i.device.address for i in listener.found] == ["BB"]


@pytest.fixture
def scanners(monkeypatch):
    """The scanners local adapters open: their arguments, in order."""
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module

    opened: list[dict] = []

    class Scanner:
        def __init__(self, detection_callback=None, scanning_mode="active", bluez=None, **kwargs):
            self.args = {
                "mode": scanning_mode,
                "patterns": (bluez or {}).get("or_patterns"),
                "on_detection": detection_callback,
                "scanning": False,
            }

        async def start(self):
            if self.args["mode"] == "passive" and opened and opened[-1].get("refuse_passive"):
                raise RuntimeError("passive scanning needs BlueZ's advertisement monitor")
            self.args["scanning"] = True
            opened.append(self.args)

        async def stop(self):
            self.args["scanning"] = False

    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "BleakScanner", Scanner)
    return opened


async def test_local_adapters_hear_every_advertiser_and_the_matchers_choose(scanners):
    from bleak.assigned_numbers import AdvertisementDataType as T
    from bleak.backends.device import BLEDevice
    from bleak.backends.scanner import AdvertisementData

    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    ble = BLEService(sources=[LocalAdapter("hci0")])
    matter, everything = Listener(), Listener()
    ble.register(matter, {MATTER})
    ble.register(everything, [BLEMatcher()])
    await ble.start()
    assert scanners[-1]["mode"] == "passive"
    assert scanners[-1]["patterns"] == [(0, T.FLAGS, b"\x02"), (0, T.FLAGS, b"\x06"), (0, T.FLAGS, b"\x1a")]

    hear = scanners[-1]["on_detection"]
    hear(BLEDevice("AA", None, {}), AdvertisementData(None, {APPLE: b"\x10\x05"}, {}, [], None, -60, ()))
    hear(BLEDevice("BB", None, {}), AdvertisementData(None, {}, {str(MATTER): b"\x00"}, [], None, -60, ()))
    await settle()
    assert [i.device.address for i in matter.found] == ["BB"]
    assert len(everything.found) == 2
    await ble.stop()


async def test_local_adapters_scan_passively_and_actively_in_bursts(scanners):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    ble = BLEService(sources=[LocalAdapter("hci0")])
    await ble.start()
    assert scanners[-1]["mode"] == "passive"

    await ble.scan_actively(0.05)  # a pairing window: names come in scan responses
    assert scanners[-1]["mode"] == "active"
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    assert scanners[-1]["mode"] == "passive"
    await ble.stop()


async def test_an_adapter_without_passive_scanning_scans_actively(scanners, caplog):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    ble = BLEService(sources=[LocalAdapter("hci0")])
    await ble.start()
    await ble.scan_actively(0.01)
    scanners[-1]["refuse_passive"] = True
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)  # the burst ends: back to passive, refused
    assert scanners[-1]["mode"] == "active"
    assert "can't scan passively" in caplog.text
    await ble.stop()


async def test_a_rescan_waits_until_a_local_adapter_has_connected(scanners, monkeypatch):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    connecting, connected = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()

    class Client:
        def __init__(self, device, **kwargs):
            pass

        async def connect(self):
            connecting.set()
            await connected.wait()

    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "BleakClient", Client)
    ble = BLEService(sources=[LocalAdapter("hci0")])
    await ble.start()
    connection = asyncio.create_task(ble.connect("AA"))
    await connecting.wait()
    burst = asyncio.create_task(ble.scan_actively(1))  # a pairing window opens meanwhile
    await settle()
    assert not any(s["scanning"] for s in scanners), "discovering while connecting: many adapters stall"

    connected.set()
    await connection
    await burst
    assert [s["mode"] for s in scanners if s["scanning"]] == ["active"]
    await ble.stop()


class ScanModeFakeBLESource(FakeBLESource):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.modes: list[bool] = []

    async def set_scan_mode(self, is_active: bool):
        self.modes.append(is_active)


async def test_a_pairing_window_switches_every_source_that_can_to_active_scanning():
    radio = ScanModeFakeBLESource("hci0")
    ble = BLEService(sources=[radio, FakeBLESource("proxy")])  # one that can't switch is left as it is
    await ble.start()
    assert radio.modes == [False]  # passive from the start

    await ble.scan_actively(0.02)
    assert radio.modes == [False, True]
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    assert radio.modes == [False, True, False]
    await ble.stop()


async def test_a_proxy_without_a_free_connection_slot_is_tried_last():
    full = FakeBLESource("full", connection=Mock(spec=BLEConnection), free_slots=0)
    free = FakeBLESource("free", connection=Mock(spec=BLEConnection), free_slots=2)
    ble = BLEService(sources=[full, free])
    await ble.start()
    full.advertise("AA", rssi=-40)
    free.advertise("AA", rssi=-80)
    await settle()

    await ble.connect("AA")
    assert (full.connected, free.connected) == ([], ["AA"])
    await ble.stop()


async def test_the_router_hears_through_the_proxies_an_integration_brings_along(tmp_path):
    from support import changed, run

    from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import BLEProxy, Need
    from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakePeripheral

    ble, proxy = BLEService(), FakeBLESource("esphome:aa")
    esphome = FakePeripheral("esphome", [Need("ble", ["router"], is_required=False)], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, ble, esphome)

    esphome.provided.append(BLEProxy(proxy, name="aa:bb"))  # a node connected, known by its Bluetooth MAC
    await changed(runtime, esphome)
    assert proxy.on_advertisement is not None  # heard through
    assert runtime.peripheral("esphome/aa:bb") is esphome.provided[0]

    again = FakeBLESource("esphome:aa")  # it reconnected: another source under the same name
    esphome.provided[:] = [BLEProxy(again)]
    await changed(runtime, esphome)
    assert proxy.on_advertisement is None and again.on_advertisement is not None

    esphome.provided.clear()  # gone
    await changed(runtime, esphome)
    assert again.on_advertisement is None


async def test_a_manufacturer_id_alone_selects_devices_that_advertise_no_service(radios):
    """Ported from feature/ble-manufacturer-filter: HomeKit (HAP-BLE) accessories advertise Apple manufacturer data
    and no service UUID."""
    ble, near, _ = radios
    by_service, by_manufacturer = Listener(), Listener()
    ble.register(by_service, {MATTER})
    ble.register(by_manufacturer, [BLEMatcher(manufacturer_id=APPLE)])

    near.advertise("AA", service_uuids=[str(MATTER)])
    near.advertise("BB", manufacturer_data={APPLE: b"\x06\x31"})
    near.advertise("CC", manufacturer_data={0x0059: b"\x01"})
    await settle()
    assert [i.device.address for i in by_service.found] == ["AA"]
    assert [i.device.address for i in by_manufacturer.found] == ["BB"]


async def test_changed_manufacturer_data_is_an_update(radios):
    ble, near, _ = radios
    listener = Listener()
    ble.register(listener, [BLEMatcher(manufacturer_id=APPLE)])

    for data in (b"\x06\x31\x01", b"\x06\x31\x01", b"\x06\x31\x02"):
        near.advertise("BB", manufacturer_data={APPLE: data})
        await settle()
    assert (len(listener.found), len(listener.updated)) == (1, 1)

# FILE: tests/runtime/test_defaults.py
================================================================================
"""What runs by default, and that it is there without the extras."""

import subprocess
import sys

from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import Compose, UsbScanner, default_peripherals, default_usb_drivers
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.builtin import otbr, silabs_multiprotocol

WITHOUT_EXTRAS = """
import importlib.abc, sys

class Missing(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder):
    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
        if name.split(".")[0] in {"serial", "bleak", "dbus_fast", "zeroconf", "typer_shell", "rich"}:
            raise ImportError(f"No module named {name!r}")

sys.meta_path.insert(0, Missing())
import majordom_integration_sdk, majordom_integration_sdk.dev, majordom_integration_sdk.testing
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import default_peripherals
print(" ".join(p.name for p in default_peripherals()))
"""


def test_the_defaults_are_what_runs_around_integrations_in_the_order_they_bind():
    assert [p.name for p in default_peripherals()] == [
        "usb",
        "bluetooth-adapters",
        "host",
        "compose",
        "silabs-multiprotocol",
        "otbr",
        "ble-router",
        "zeroconf",
        "ssdp",
    ]
    on_demand = [p.name for p in default_peripherals() if p.is_on_demand]
    assert on_demand == ["compose", "silabs-multiprotocol", "otbr", "ble-router", "zeroconf", "ssdp"]


def test_the_containers_listen_where_the_host_says():
    assert next(p for p in default_peripherals() if isinstance(p, Compose)).listen_address == "127.0.0.1"
    lab = default_peripherals(listen_address="0.0.0.0")  # a lab harness reached from another host
    assert next(p for p in lab if isinstance(p, Compose)).listen_address == "0.0.0.0"


def test_the_usb_scanner_knows_every_sdk_driver_by_default():
    assert [driver.name for driver in default_usb_drivers()] == ["zwave", "silabs"]  # the cheap Z-Wave check first
    assert [driver.name for driver in UsbScanner().drivers] == ["zwave", "silabs"]
    scanner = next(p for p in default_peripherals() if isinstance(p, UsbScanner))
    assert [driver.name for driver in scanner.drivers] == ["zwave", "silabs"]


def test_every_runtime_gets_defaults_of_its_own():
    first, second = default_peripherals(), default_peripherals()
    assert not {id(p) for p in first} & {id(p) for p in second}
    assert otbr() is not otbr() and silabs_multiprotocol() is not silabs_multiprotocol()
    assert not {id(d) for d in default_usb_drivers()} & {id(d) for d in default_usb_drivers()}
    assert not {id(d) for d in UsbScanner().drivers} & {id(d) for d in UsbScanner().drivers}


def test_the_package_and_its_defaults_import_without_the_extras():
    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", WITHOUT_EXTRAS], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    assert result.stdout.split() == [
        "usb",
        "bluetooth-adapters",
        "host",
        "compose",
        "silabs-multiprotocol",
        "otbr",
        "ble-router",
        "ssdp",
    ]
    assert 'pip install "majordom-integration-sdk[discovery]"' in result.stderr  # no DNS-SD, said once
