"""Containers as peripherals: what they render, the ports they get, when they are ready, what they learn."""

import asyncio
import json
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest
import yaml
from pydantic import BaseModel
from support import changed, run, settle, state, until

from majordom_integration_sdk import Endpoint, Need, Platform, Service
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import PeripheralState, PeripheralStatus
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import StatusKind as K
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services import builtin
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose import Compose
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakeCompose, FakePeripheral, RecordingRuntimeOutput

IP = Endpoint("ip", is_shared=True)
MULTIPAN = Endpoint("multipan", "silabs-cpc", "/dev/ttyUSB0", params={"baud": 460800, "flow_control": True})
NCP = Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "/dev/ttyUSB1", params={"baud": 115200, "flow_control": True})
RCP = Endpoint("thread", "spinel", "/dev/ttyUSB2", params={"baud": 460800, "flow_control": True})


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def listening(monkeypatch) -> set[int]:
    """Host ports something listens on; none unless a test says so."""
    ports: set[int] = set()
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose._is_listening", ports.__contains__
    )
    return ports


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def no_thread_network(monkeypatch):
    """The built-in border routers form and read no real network."""

    async def nothing(*args: Any):
        return None

    for talking in ("join_network", "active_dataset", "network_channel", "move_channel"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(builtin, talking, nothing)


def host() -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("host", provides=[IP])


def stick(name: str, *provides: Endpoint) -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral(name, provides=provides)


def zigbee() -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")])


def matter(**compose: Any) -> tuple[FakePeripheral, Service]:
    server = Service(
        "matterjs-server",
        compose={"image": "matter", "environment": {"OTBR": "{peripherals.thread.url}"} | compose},
        needs=[Need("ip"), Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"], is_required=False)],
        provides=[Endpoint("matter", "matter-server-ws", "ws://127.0.0.1:{ports.api}/ws")],
        ports={"api": 5580},
    )
    return FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("matter", ["matter-server-ws"])]), server


def compose(tmp_path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads((tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals" / "compose" / "compose.json").read_text())["services"]


async def test_a_multipan_stick_serves_zigbee_and_matter_through_one_container(tmp_path):
    radio, integration, (app, server), otbr = stick("sky", MULTIPAN), zigbee(), matter(), builtin.otbr()
    peripherals = (host(), radio, builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), otbr, integration, server, app)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)

    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "socket://127.0.0.1:9999")
    assert app.peripherals.endpoint("matter").url == "ws://127.0.0.1:5580/ws"
    services = compose(tmp_path)
    assert set(services) == {"silabs-multiprotocol", "matterjs-server"}  # no one binds the standalone border router
    assert services["silabs-multiprotocol"]["devices"][0] == "/dev/ttyUSB0:/dev/ttyRCP"
    environment = services["silabs-multiprotocol"]["environment"]
    assert (environment["RADIO_BAUD"], environment["RADIO_FLOW_CONTROL"]) == ("460800", "True")
    assert services["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["OTBR"] == "http://127.0.0.1:8081"
    assert "depends_on" not in services["matterjs-server"]  # its border router coming and going doesn't restart it
    assert runtime.users(radio) == ["silabs-multiprotocol", "zigbee", "matterjs-server", "matter"]
    assert runtime.uses(app) == ["matterjs-server", "host", "silabs-multiprotocol", "compose", "sky"]
    assert runtime.reach([MULTIPAN]) == ["thread", "zigbee"]  # through the containers it would run
    assert runtime.status(otbr) == PeripheralStatus(
        PeripheralState.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, "need thread/spinel: nothing offers it"
    )


async def test_learning_the_thread_network_recreates_no_border_router(tmp_path):
    containers = FakeCompose()
    network = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", thread_dataset="0e08hub")
    peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), zigbee())
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, *peripherals, platform=network)
    applied = len(containers.calls)

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(network, thread_dataset="0e08learned"))  # provisioned onto it instead
    await settle(runtime)
    assert containers.calls[applied:] == []


async def test_split_radios_use_direct_zigbee_and_a_standalone_border_router(tmp_path):
    ncp, rcp, integration, (app, server) = stick("ncp", NCP), stick("rcp", RCP), zigbee(), matter()
    peripherals = (host(), ncp, rcp, builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), builtin.otbr(), integration, server, app)
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)

    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == NCP
    assert set(compose(tmp_path)) == {"otbr", "matterjs-server"}
    assert compose(tmp_path)["otbr"]["devices"][0] == "/dev/ttyUSB2:/dev/ttyRCP"
    rcp_url = "spinel+hdlc+uart:///dev/ttyRCP?uart-baudrate=460800&uart-flow-control"
    assert compose(tmp_path)["otbr"]["environment"]["OT_RCP_DEVICE"] == rcp_url


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("router", "radio", "listening"),
    [(builtin.silabs_multiprotocol, MULTIPAN, "LISTEN_ADDRESS"), (builtin.otbr, RCP, "OT_REST_LISTEN_ADDR")],
)
async def test_a_border_router_answers_only_the_hub_unless_the_host_listens_on_the_lan(
    tmp_path, router, radio, listening
):
    service, matter = router(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), stick("radio", radio), service, matter)
    assert compose(tmp_path)[service.name]["environment"][listening] == "127.0.0.1"  # over loopback, on the host

    lab, service, matter = tmp_path / "lab", router(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    containers = FakeCompose(listen_address="0.0.0.0")  # a lab harness: no password guards it
    await run(lab, containers, host(), stick("radio", radio), service, matter)
    assert compose(lab)[service.name]["environment"][listening] == "0.0.0.0"
    assert "is_exposed_on_lan" not in service.Settings.model_fields  # the host's switch, not the user's


def test_the_harness_runs_matterjs_server_on_loopback_without_logging_the_thread_key():
    # at info matter.js logs every command's fields, the Thread network key among them; the LAN only for a lab harness
    harness = yaml.safe_load((builtin._IMAGES / "multiprotocol" / "docker-compose.yml").read_text())
    environment = harness["services"]["matterjs-server"]["environment"]
    assert (environment["LISTEN_ADDRESS"], environment["LOG_LEVEL"]) == ("${LISTEN_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}", "warning")


async def test_a_container_keeps_its_data_in_its_documents_folder(tmp_path):
    otbr, matter = builtin.otbr(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), stick("rcp", RCP), otbr, matter)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["otbr"]["volumes"][0] == f"{tmp_path}/data/peripherals/otbr:/data"
    assert (tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals" / "otbr").is_dir()


async def test_the_folders_a_container_binds_from_its_data_are_created_before_docker_would_as_root(tmp_path):
    # a factory reset then removes what the container wrote in them through Docker, and the folders as the hub's user
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), zigbee())
    data = tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals" / "silabs-multiprotocol"
    assert sorted(path.name for path in data.iterdir()) == ["thread", "zigbee"]


async def test_a_wipe_empties_a_service_s_data_through_docker_in_its_own_image(tmp_path):
    # its container wrote there as root, which the hub's user can't remove (a factory reset): the Thread network
    containers, otbr, matter = FakeCompose(), builtin.otbr(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, host(), stick("rcp", RCP), otbr, matter)
    data = otbr.platform.documents_folder(otbr)
    (data / "0_a5c.data").write_text("dataset")
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="runs"):
        await containers.wipe(otbr)  # its container would write on

    await runtime.stop()
    applied = len(containers.calls)
    await containers.wipe(otbr)
    assert containers.calls[applied:] == [
        ("run", "--rm", "--pull", "never", "--network", "none", "--userns", "host", "--user", "0", "--entrypoint")
        + ("find", "-v", f"{data}:/d", otbr.compose["image"], "/d", "-mindepth", "1", "-delete")
    ]

    (data / "0_a5c.data").unlink()
    await containers.wipe(otbr)
    assert len(containers.calls) == applied + 1  # nothing to remove: no container run


async def test_without_radios_zigbee_waits_and_matter_runs_over_ip(tmp_path):
    integration, (app, server) = zigbee(), matter()
    peripherals = (host(), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), builtin.otbr(), integration, server, app)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)

    assert state(runtime, integration) == PeripheralState.WAITING
    assert state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.RUNNING
    assert compose(tmp_path)["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["OTBR"] == ""


async def test_an_endpoint_given_first_replaces_the_border_router(tmp_path):
    mine = stick("pinned", Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest", "http://mine:8081", is_shared=True))
    app, server = matter()
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), mine, host(), stick("rcp", RCP), builtin.otbr(), server, app)

    assert set(compose(tmp_path)) == {"matterjs-server"}
    assert compose(tmp_path)["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["OTBR"] == "http://mine:8081"


async def test_a_disabled_integration_takes_its_container_down(tmp_path):
    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), server, app)
    assert set(compose(tmp_path)) == {"matterjs-server"}

    await runtime.disable(app)
    assert compose(tmp_path) == {}


class Keys(BaseModel):
    key: str = "secret"


async def test_a_service_setting_recreates_only_that_service(tmp_path):
    zwave_server = Service(
        "zwave-js-server",
        compose={"image": "zwave", "environment": {"KEY": "{settings.key}"}},
        needs=[Need("ip")],
        provides=[Endpoint("zwave", "zwave-js-ws", "ws://127.0.0.1:3000")],
        settings=Keys,
    )
    zwave = FakePeripheral("zwave", [Need("zwave")])
    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), zwave_server, zwave, server, app)
    before = compose(tmp_path)
    assert before["zwave-js-server"]["environment"]["KEY"] == "secret"

    await runtime.update_settings(zwave_server, {"key": "other"})
    await settle(runtime)
    after = compose(tmp_path)
    assert {name for name in before if before[name] != after[name]} == {"zwave-js-server"}
    assert zwave.calls == ["start"]  # what it is bound to is the same: it reconnects on its own


async def test_the_rendered_containers_and_the_settings_are_kept_from_other_users(tmp_path):
    keys = Service(
        "zwave-js-server", {"environment": {"KEY": "{settings.key}"}}, provides=[Endpoint("zwave")], settings=Keys
    )
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), keys, FakePeripheral("zwave", [Need("zwave")]))  # its network keys
    assert compose(tmp_path)["zwave-js-server"]["environment"] == {"KEY": "secret"}
    for kept in (tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals" / "compose" / "compose.json", tmp_path / "data" / "state.json"):
        assert kept.stat().st_mode & 0o777 == 0o600


async def test_a_moved_need_recreates_a_service_only_when_it_renders_otherwise(tmp_path):
    containers, radio = FakeCompose(), stick("sky", NCP)
    bridge = Service("bridge", {"devices": ["{peripherals.zigbee.url}:/dev/ttyRCP"]}, [Need("zigbee")], [Endpoint("b")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, radio, bridge, FakePeripheral("user", [Need("b")]))
    applied = len(containers.calls)

    radio.provided = [replace(NCP, params={"baud": 57600})]  # moved, but what it renders is the same
    await changed(runtime, radio)
    assert containers.calls[applied:] == [] and state(runtime, bridge) == PeripheralState.RUNNING

    radio.provided = [replace(NCP, url="/dev/ttyUSB9")]
    await changed(runtime, radio)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["bridge"]["devices"] == ["/dev/ttyUSB9:/dev/ttyRCP"]


async def test_the_platform_facts_render_and_a_change_recreates_only_what_renders_them(tmp_path):
    before, containers = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", region="Europe"), FakeCompose()
    app, server = matter(REGION="{platform.region}")
    plain = Service("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("plain")], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, host(), server, app, plain, user, platform=before)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "Europe"
    applied = len(containers.calls)

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(before, region="USA"))
    await settle(runtime)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "USA"
    assert len([call for call in containers.calls[applied:] if "-f" in call]) == 2  # without it, then with it again
    assert runtime.status(server).state == PeripheralState.RUNNING
    assert app.changes == user.changes == [("platform", before)]  # the integrations hear it too


async def test_a_service_renders_only_when_it_is_created(tmp_path):
    class InPlace(Service):
        async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before: Platform) -> bool:
            return True  # it takes the region over its API

    europe = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", region="Europe")
    radio = InPlace(
        "radio", {"image": "radio", "environment": {"REGION": "{platform.region}"}}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("r")]
    )
    plain = Service("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("r"), Need("plain")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), radio, plain, user, platform=europe)

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(europe, region="USA"))
    await runtime.restart(plain)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["radio"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "Europe"  # not recreated behind its back


async def test_a_container_still_starting_is_recreated_once_it_serves_only_if_the_facts_render_it(tmp_path):
    gate, containers, created = asyncio.Event(), FakeCompose(), set()
    europe = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", region="Europe")

    class Slow(Service):
        async def is_healthy(self) -> bool:
            created.add(self.name)
            await gate.wait()
            return True

    environment = {"REGION": "{platform.region}"}
    renders = Slow("renders", {"image": "r", "environment": environment}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("r")])
    plain = Slow("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("r"), Need("plain")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, host(), renders, plain, user, settled=False, platform=europe)
    await until(runtime, lambda: created == {"renders", "plain"}, settled=False)
    applied = len(containers.calls)

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(europe, region="USA"))
    gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["renders"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "USA"
    assert len([call for call in containers.calls[applied:] if "-f" in call]) == 2  # renders' only: down, then up
    assert state(runtime, user) == PeripheralState.RUNNING


async def test_services_get_free_host_ports_and_keep_them(tmp_path, listening):
    async def ezsp() -> tuple[str, str]:
        """The zigbee URL bound after a (re)boot, and the port the container got."""
        integration = zigbee()
        peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), integration)
        runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)
        port = compose(tmp_path)["silabs-multiprotocol"]["environment"]["EZSP_TCP_PORT"]
        await runtime.stop()
        return integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee").url, port

    assert await ezsp() == ("socket://127.0.0.1:9999", "9999")  # the preferred port, free

    listening.add(9999)  # after a reboot something else took it before our container came up
    moved, port = await ezsp()
    assert moved == f"socket://127.0.0.1:{port}" != "socket://127.0.0.1:9999"

    listening.clear()  # the preferred port is free again: the service stays where it is now
    assert (await ezsp())[0] == moved


async def test_a_port_held_by_our_own_running_container_is_kept(tmp_path, listening, monkeypatch):
    peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol())
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals, zigbee())
    await runtime.stop()
    listening.update({9999, 8081})  # our silabs-multiprotocol container is up and holds them

    async def containers(self) -> set[str]:
        return {"silabs-multiprotocol"}

    monkeypatch.setattr(Compose, "_containers", containers)
    integration = zigbee()
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals, integration)
    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee").url == "socket://127.0.0.1:9999"


async def test_services_preferring_the_same_port_get_different_ones(tmp_path):
    bridge = Service(
        "bridge",
        {"image": "bridge", "command": ["--port", "{ports.api}"]},
        provides=[Endpoint("bridge", "x", "ws://127.0.0.1:{ports.api}")],
        ports={"api": 5580},
    )
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("bridge")])
    app, server = matter()
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), server, app, bridge, user)
    api = compose(tmp_path)["bridge"]["command"][1]
    assert user.peripherals.endpoint("bridge").url == f"ws://127.0.0.1:{api}"
    ports = {api, app.peripherals.endpoint("matter").url.rsplit(":", 1)[1].removesuffix("/ws")}
    assert len(ports) == 2 and "5580" in ports  # one got the port both prefer, the other another


class Router(Service):
    """A border router that is set up once it answers and knows its Thread network."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("router", {"image": "router"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("thread", "rest", "http://ours")])
        self.release, self.calls = asyncio.Event(), []

    async def provision(self, endpoint: Endpoint):
        await self.release.wait()
        self.calls.append(("provision", endpoint.url))

    async def start(self):
        await super().start()
        self.calls.append(("learn", "http://ours"))
        await self.output.peripheral_did_learn(self, {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})


async def test_what_needs_a_service_waits_for_its_setup_then_hears_what_it_learned(tmp_path):
    router, output = Router(), RecordingRuntimeOutput()
    thread = FakePeripheral("thread", [Need("thread")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), router, thread, output=output, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, router) == PeripheralState.STARTING, settled=False)
    assert runtime.status(thread) == PeripheralStatus(PeripheralState.WAITING, K.NEEDS_STARTING, "waiting for router")

    await runtime.refresh()  # something else changed meanwhile: its setup goes on
    router.release.set()
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, thread) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    assert router.calls == [("provision", "http://ours"), ("learn", "http://ours")]
    assert output.learned == [("router", {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})]

    await runtime.restart(router)  # recreated: it may hold another network now
    await until(runtime, lambda: len(output.learned) == 2)
    assert router.calls[-2:] == [("provision", "http://ours"), ("learn", "http://ours")]
    assert thread.calls == ["start"]


class Docker:
    """Docker, faked: ``calls`` it got; a container runs once applied, and its ports answer while ``is_answering``.
    Applying fails while ``failure`` is set; it isn't reachable unless ``is_reachable``, can't tell what runs unless
    ``is_listing``."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, ...]] = []
        self.applied: list[set[str]] = []  # the services of each compose file it took
        self.composes: list[Compose] = []
        self.is_answering = self.is_reachable = self.is_listing = True
        self.left_running: set[str] = set()  # containers that outlived the runtime that ran them
        self.failure = b""
        self.gate: asyncio.Event | None = None  # while set, applying waits for it

    async def exec(self, *args: str, **kwargs: Any) -> "Process":
        self.calls.append(args)
        if "info" in args:
            return Process(b"", 0 if self.is_reachable else 1)
        if "ps" in args:
            running = "\n".join({*self.left_running, *(name for c in self.composes for name in c._running)})
            return Process(running.encode(), 0 if self.is_listing else 1)
        self.applied.append(set(json.loads(Path(args[args.index("-f") + 1]).read_text())["services"]))
        return Process(self.failure, 1 if self.failure else 0, self.gate)

    def holds(self, port: int) -> bool:
        running = (
            ports for compose in self.composes for name, ports in compose.ports.items() if name in compose._running
        )
        return self.is_answering and any(port in ports.values() for ports in running)


class Process:
    def __init__(self, output: bytes, returncode: int, gate: asyncio.Event | None = None):
        self.output, self.returncode, self.gate = output, returncode, gate

    async def communicate(self) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
        if self.gate:
            await self.gate.wait()
        return self.output, b""


@pytest.fixture
def docker(monkeypatch, listening) -> Docker:
    docker, init = Docker(), Compose.__init__

    def record(self):
        init(self)
        docker.composes.append(self)

    monkeypatch.setattr(Compose, "__init__", record)
    monkeypatch.setattr("asyncio.create_subprocess_exec", docker.exec)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose._is_listening",
        lambda port: port in listening or docker.holds(port),
    )
    return docker


async def test_without_docker_the_services_wait_saying_so(tmp_path, docker):
    docker.is_reachable = False
    app, server = matter()
    containers = Compose()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, host(), server, app)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, containers) == PeripheralState.FAILED)
    assert runtime.status(containers).detail.startswith("Docker isn't reachable: docker info")
    reason = "need matter/matter-server-ws: matterjs-server can't run (need container/compose: compose is failed)"
    assert runtime.status(app) == PeripheralStatus(PeripheralState.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, reason)


async def test_a_port_stays_while_docker_cant_tell_what_runs(tmp_path, docker, listening):
    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app)
    await runtime.stop()
    listening.add(5580)  # our container is still up after the hub restarted: it holds its port
    docker.left_running.add("matterjs-server")
    docker.is_listing = False

    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app)
    assert state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.WAITING
    docker.is_listing = True
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    assert app.peripherals.endpoint("matter").url == "ws://127.0.0.1:5580/ws"


async def test_a_failed_compose_up_is_tried_again(tmp_path, docker):
    docker.failure = b"Conflict. The container name is already in use"
    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app)
    assert runtime.status(server).state == PeripheralState.WAITING
    assert "Conflict. The container name is already in use" in runtime.status(server).detail

    docker.failure = b""
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    assert [call[-3:] for call in docker.calls if "-f" in call] == [("up", "-d", "--remove-orphans")] * 2


async def test_a_container_is_ready_once_compose_runs_it_and_its_ports_answer(tmp_path, docker):
    docker.is_answering = False
    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, server) == PeripheralState.STARTING, settled=False)
    assert runtime.status(app).detail == "waiting for matterjs-server"

    docker.is_answering = True
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)


async def test_a_container_that_never_answers_fails_its_start(tmp_path, docker):
    docker.is_answering = False
    app, server = matter()
    server.start_timeout = 0.05
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, server) == PeripheralState.FAILED)
    assert runtime.status(server) == PeripheralStatus(PeripheralState.FAILED, K.GAVE_UP, "didn't start within 0.05 s")
    assert runtime.status(app).detail == "need matter/matter-server-ws: matterjs-server is failed"


async def test_restarting_a_service_recreates_only_its_container(tmp_path, docker):
    app, server = matter()
    integration = zigbee()
    peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), integration, server, app)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), *peripherals)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == state(runtime, integration) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    before = compose(tmp_path)

    await runtime.restart(server)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, server) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    assert compose(tmp_path) == before
    assert [call[-1] for call in docker.calls if "-f" in call][-2:] == ["--remove-orphans"] * 2  # without, with it
    assert (app.calls, integration.calls) == (["start"], ["start"])


async def test_a_container_whose_start_was_stopped_is_taken_down(tmp_path, docker):
    app, server = matter()
    plain = Service("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("plain")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)

    docker.gate = asyncio.Event()
    runtime.given += [plain, user]
    refresh = asyncio.ensure_future(runtime.refresh())
    await until(runtime, lambda: docker.applied[-1] == {"matterjs-server", "plain"}, settled=False)
    asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(0.05, docker.gate.set)  # docker takes it after all
    await runtime.disable(user)
    await refresh
    await settle(runtime)
    assert docker.applied[-1] == {"matterjs-server"}

import asyncio
import contextlib
import json
import threading
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import replace
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler
from socketserver import ThreadingTCPServer
from typing import Any, cast

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk import Endpoint, Peripheral, Peripherals, Service
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services import builtin as services
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.builtin import (
    active_dataset,
    join_network,
    move_channel,
    network_channel,
    otbr,
    silabs_multiprotocol,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import RecordingPeripheralOutput, build_test_platform


def dataset(network: str, channel: int = 15) -> str:
    """An active dataset's hex TLVs: its timestamp, channel and Extended PAN ID (the network)."""
    return f"0e080000000000010000000300{channel:04x}0208{network}"


HUB, OTHER = dataset("dead00beef00cafe"), dataset("0123456789abcdef")
ENABLE, DISABLE = ("/node/state", json.dumps("enable")), ("/node/state", json.dumps("disable"))
PENDING = "/node/dataset/pending"


def rest(url: str) -> Endpoint:
    return Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest", url, is_shared=True)


@pytest.fixture
def border_router():
    """A border router's REST API with no network until one is put, and no change of it pending: one put lands at
    once, one pending while ``landing`` lands right after its active dataset is read. It refuses puts to the path
    ``refused`` names, and fails each put in ``failing`` once."""
    state: dict[str, Any] = {"dataset": "", "pending": "", "thread": "leader", "puts": [], "failing": []}

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def do_GET(self):
            read = {PENDING: state["pending"], "/node/state": json.dumps(state["thread"])}
            body = read.get(self.path, state["dataset"]).encode()
            self.send_response(200 if body else 204)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)
            if self.path == "/node/dataset/active" and state.get("landing"):
                state["dataset"], state["pending"], state["landing"] = state["pending"], "", False

        def do_PUT(self):
            body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])).decode()
            state["puts"].append((self.path, body))
            if self.path == state.get("refused") or (self.path, body) in state["failing"]:
                with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
                    state["failing"].remove((self.path, body))
                self.send_response(409)
                self.end_headers()
                return
            if self.path == "/node/state":
                state["thread"] = "disabled" if body == json.dumps("disable") else "leader"
            if self.path == "/node/dataset/active" and not state.get("stuck"):
                state["dataset"] = body if body.startswith("0e") else "0e08newnetwork"
            elif self.path == PENDING:
                state["dataset"] = body  # its delay passed
            self.send_response(200)
            self.end_headers()

        def log_message(self, format, *args):
            pass

    server = ThreadingTCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)  # HTTPServer would resolve the host name first
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, args=(0.01,), daemon=True).start()
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}", state
    server.shutdown()
    server.server_close()


async def test_returns_the_network_someone_else_formed(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = "0e08existing"
    assert await active_dataset(url) == "0e08existing"
    await join_network(url, None)
    assert state["puts"] == []


async def test_forms_a_network_when_none_appears(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    await join_network(url, None, patience=0)
    assert await active_dataset(url) == "0e08newnetwork"
    assert state["puts"] == [("/node/dataset/active", json.dumps({"NetworkName": "MajorDom"})), ENABLE]


async def test_joins_the_given_network(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    await join_network(url, "0e08given", patience=0)
    assert await active_dataset(url) == "0e08given"


async def test_joins_the_given_network_in_place_of_another_it_has(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = OTHER  # its container formed one before the hub's was known
    await join_network(url, HUB)
    assert state["puts"] == [DISABLE, ("/node/dataset/active", HUB), ENABLE]  # written only while Thread is off


async def test_a_join_whose_enable_failed_once_turns_thread_on_when_tried_again(border_router):

    state["dataset"], state["failing"] = OTHER, [ENABLE]  # otbr-agent busy a moment

    assert state["puts"] == [DISABLE, ("/node/dataset/active", HUB), ENABLE, ENABLE]
    assert state["thread"] == "leader"

    assert state["puts"][-2:] == [ENABLE, ENABLE] and state["thread"] == "leader"


async def test_keeps_the_given_network_after_it_moved(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20)  # the same network, on another channel since
    await join_network(url, HUB)
    assert state["puts"] == []


async def test_forms_only_once(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["stuck"] = True  # forming takes a while: the dataset doesn't appear yet
    await asyncio.wait_for(join_network(url, None, patience=0), 3)
    assert len(state["puts"]) == 2  # one dataset, one enable
    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
        await asyncio.wait_for(active_dataset(url), 0.2)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("router", "formed"), [(otbr, ""), (silabs_multiprotocol, OTHER)])
async def test_a_border_router_is_provisioned_onto_the_hubs_thread_network(border_router, monkeypatch, router, formed):
    url, state = border_router
    monkeypatch.setattr(services, "FORM_PATIENCE", 0)
    state["dataset"] = formed  # the multiprotocol container forms one of its own, as it warms the radio up
    service = serving(router(), url, thread_dataset=HUB)  # learned from the stick before
    await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)
    assert await active_dataset(url) == HUB
    assert PENDING not in [path for path, _ in state["puts"]]  # on the same channel


async def test_a_multiprotocol_router_moves_the_network_it_joins_to_zigbees_channel(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = dataset("0123456789abcdef", channel=15)  # its container formed it on Zigbee's channel
    service = serving(silabs_multiprotocol(), url, thread_dataset=dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20))
    await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)

    assert state["puts"][1] == ("/node/dataset/active", service.platform.thread_dataset)  # joined
    pending = dict(state["puts"])[PENDING]  # the devices on it follow: new active and pending timestamps, a delay
    assert "000300000f" in pending and "0208dead00beef00cafe" in pending and "3308" in pending and "3404" in pending


async def test_a_change_pending_on_another_network_moves_nothing_of_the_one_it_joins(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    restored = dataset("0123456789abcdef", channel=15)
    state["dataset"] = state["pending"] = restored  # a move of the network it restored, left pending
    service = serving(silabs_multiprotocol(), url, thread_dataset=dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20))
    await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)

    assert "000300000f" in dict(state["puts"])[PENDING]  # the hub's network moved to Zigbee's channel all the same
    assert learned(service) == [(service, {"thread_dataset": state["dataset"]})]


async def test_a_channel_move_that_cant_land_fails_the_start(border_router, monkeypatch):
    url, state = border_router
    monkeypatch.setattr(services, "FORM_PATIENCE", 0.1)
    state["dataset"], state["refused"] = dataset("0123456789abcdef", channel=15), PENDING  # e.g. not attached
    service = serving(silabs_multiprotocol(), url, thread_dataset=dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20))
    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match="channel 15"):
        await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)
    assert learned(service) == []


async def test_a_standalone_router_keeps_the_channel_of_the_network_it_joins(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = dataset("0123456789abcdef", channel=15)
    service = serving(otbr(), url, thread_dataset=dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20))
    await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)
    assert PENDING not in [path for path, _ in state["puts"]]


def test_a_move_is_stamped_after_the_network_it_moves_with_the_clock_behind(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(services.time, "time", lambda: 1000)  # a Pi without a clock of its own, before NTP
    stamped = (2_000_000_000 << 16).to_bytes(8).hex()  # by an earlier move, with the clock right
    moved = services._tlvs(services._moved(f"0e08{stamped}000300000f0208dead00beef00cafe", 20))
    assert int.from_bytes(moved[services._ACTIVE_TIMESTAMP]) >> 16 == 2_000_000_001  # newer: the devices take it
    assert moved[services._PENDING_TIMESTAMP] == moved[services._ACTIVE_TIMESTAMP]


async def test_the_channel_is_the_one_its_network_is_on_or_moving_to(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    reading = asyncio.create_task(network_channel(url))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    assert not reading.done()  # no network yet

    state["dataset"] = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20)
    assert await asyncio.wait_for(reading, 3) == 20
    state["pending"] = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=15)
    assert await network_channel(url) == 15


async def test_a_channel_move_is_tried_again_until_the_border_router_takes_it(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"], state["refused"] = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20), PENDING  # not attached yet
    moving = asyncio.create_task(move_channel(url, 15))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    state["refused"] = None
    await asyncio.wait_for(moving, 3)
    assert [path for path, _ in state["puts"]].count(PENDING) > 1 and "000300000f" in state["dataset"]


async def test_learns_the_network_only_once_a_channel_move_landed(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    moved = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=15)
    state["dataset"], state["pending"] = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20), moved
    learning = asyncio.create_task(active_dataset(url))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    assert not learning.done()  # Matter would commission devices onto the channel it leaves

    state["dataset"], state["pending"] = moved, ""
    assert await asyncio.wait_for(learning, 3) == moved


async def test_a_move_landing_between_two_reads_is_learned_once_landed(border_router):
    url, state = border_router
    moved = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=15)
    state["dataset"], state["pending"], state["landing"] = dataset("dead00beef00cafe", channel=20), moved, True
    assert await asyncio.wait_for(active_dataset(url), 3) == moved


class Answering:
    """Runs nothing: the border router at ``url`` answers already, and is set up as the runtime's containers are."""

    def __init__(self, url: str):
        self.url = url

    def provided(self, service: Service) -> list[Endpoint]:
        return [replace(endpoint, url=self.url) for endpoint in service.templates]

    async def up(self, service: Service):
        for endpoint in service.provides:
            await service.provision(endpoint)

    async def down(self, service: Service):
        pass

    def is_current(self, service: Service) -> bool:
        return True


def serving[S: Service](service: S, url: str, **facts: Any) -> S:
    """``service`` on the border router at ``url``, the platform holding ``facts``; what it tells recorded."""
    service.platform = build_test_platform(**facts)
    service.peripherals = Peripherals({"container": Endpoint("container", "compose", instance=Answering(url))})
    service.output = RecordingPeripheralOutput()
    return service


def learned(service: Service) -> list[tuple[Peripheral, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
    return cast(RecordingPeripheralOutput, service.output).learned


@pytest.mark.parametrize("router", [otbr, silabs_multiprotocol])
async def test_a_border_router_tells_its_thread_network_once_it_serves(border_router, router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = dataset("0123456789abcdef")
    service = serving(router(), url)
    await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)
    assert learned(service) == [(service, {"thread_dataset": dataset("0123456789abcdef")})]

# FILE: tests/runtime/test_thread_source.py

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services import builtin as services

SCRIPT = services._IMAGES / "thread-source" / "run"

# A stand-in for iproute2: answers the queries the script makes from a JSON state and applies its route changes.
FAKE_IP = f"""#!{sys.executable}
import ipaddress, json, sys
from pathlib import Path

state_file = Path(__file__).with_name("state.json")
state = json.loads(state_file.read_text())
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:5] == ["-o", "-6", "addr", "show", "dev"]:
    if args[5] not in state["addr"]:
        sys.exit(f'Device "{{args[5]}}" does not exist.')
    print("\\n".join(state["addr"][args[5]]))
elif args[:4] == ["-6", "route", "show", "match"]:
    address = ipaddress.ip_address(args[4])
    for dst, line in state["routes"].get(args[6], {{}}).items():
        if dst != "default" and address in ipaddress.ip_network(dst):
            print(f"{{dst}} {{line}}")
elif args[:3] == ["-6", "route", "replace"]:
    state["replaced"].append(args[3:])
    state["routes"][args[5]][args[3]] = " ".join(args[6:])
    state_file.write_text(json.dumps(state))
else:
    sys.exit(f"unexpected: ip {{' '.join(args)}}")
"""

ETH0 = [
    "2: eth0    inet6 fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:ce47:229:37f5:dc98/64 scope global temporary dynamic",
    "2: eth0    inet6 2a0a:a548:cced:0:8aa2:9eff:fea7:d66d/64 scope global dynamic mngtmpaddr proto kernel_ra",
    "2: eth0    inet6 fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:8aa2:9eff:fea7:d66d/64 scope global dynamic mngtmpaddr proto kernel_ra",
]
WPAN0 = [
    "7: wpan0    inet6 fd4c:60e5:af3f:4111:0:ff:fe00:fc11/64 scope global nodad deprecated",
    "7: wpan0    inet6 fd11:ec6a:d233:1:5465:34b9:c5b4:2b7c/64 scope global nodad",
    "7: wpan0    inet6 fd4c:60e5:af3f:4111:f746:74ed:1eb7:e84/64 scope global nodad deprecated",
]
OMR, MESH_LOCAL = "fd11:ec6a:d233:1::/64", "fd4c:60e5:af3f:4111::/64"
STABLE_ULA = "fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:8aa2:9eff:fea7:d66d"
KERNEL_ROUTE = "proto kernel metric 256 pref medium"


@pytest.fixture
def host(tmp_path: Path):
    """The border router's host as `ip` shows it: Thread routes as the kernel adds them for wpan0's addresses."""
    (tmp_path / "ip").write_text(FAKE_IP)
    (tmp_path / "ip").chmod(0o755)
    state = {
        "addr": {"eth0": ETH0, "wpan0": WPAN0},
        "routes": {"wpan0": {OMR: KERNEL_ROUTE, MESH_LOCAL: KERNEL_ROUTE}},
        "replaced": [],
    }
    (tmp_path / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state))
    return tmp_path


def sync(host: Path) -> dict:
    env = {"PATH": f"{host}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}", "OT_THREAD_IF": "wpan0", "BACKBONE_IF": "eth0"}
    subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", f'source "{SCRIPT}" && sync_sources'], env=env, check=True, timeout=10)
    return json.loads((host / "state.json").read_text())


def edit(host: Path, change):
    state = json.loads((host / "state.json").read_text())
    change(state)
    (host / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state))


def test_routes_to_the_border_routers_own_thread_addresses_take_a_stable_backbone_ula(host):
    state = sync(host)
    assert state["replaced"] == [[OMR, "dev", "wpan0", *KERNEL_ROUTE.split(), "src", STABLE_ULA]]
    assert MESH_LOCAL not in {r[0] for r in state["replaced"]}  # only deprecated addresses of ours there


def test_a_route_with_the_source_already_is_left_alone(host):
    sync(host)
    assert len(sync(host)["replaced"]) == 1


def test_follows_the_border_router_re_adding_its_route(host):
    sync(host)
    edit(host, lambda s: s["routes"]["wpan0"].update({OMR: KERNEL_ROUTE}))
    assert len(sync(host)["replaced"]) == 2


def test_follows_the_backbone_renumbering(host):
    sync(host)
    renumbered = "fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:1111:2222:3333:4444"
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].update(eth0=[ETH0[2].replace(STABLE_ULA, renumbered)]))
    assert sync(host)["replaced"][-1][-2:] == ["src", renumbered]


def test_a_temporary_ula_when_there_is_no_stable_one(host):
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].update(eth0=ETH0[:2]))
    assert sync(host)["replaced"][0][-1] == "fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:ce47:229:37f5:dc98"


def test_without_a_backbone_ula_nothing_changes(host):
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].update(eth0=[ETH0[1]]))  # a GUA: nodes may have no route back to it
    assert sync(host)["replaced"] == []


def test_without_a_thread_interface_nothing_changes(host):
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].pop("wpan0"))
    assert sync(host)["replaced"] == []


def test_both_border_routers_run_it():
    assert f"{SCRIPT.parent}:/etc/services.d/thread-source:ro" in services.otbr().compose["volumes"]  # s6 starts it
    assert f"{SCRIPT}:/thread-source:ro" in services.silabs_multiprotocol().compose["volumes"]
    assert "bash /thread-source &" in (services._IMAGES / "multiprotocol" / "entrypoint.sh").read_text()

# FILE: tests/runtime/test_zeroconf.py
================================================================================
"""The runtime's DNS-SD browser, over fakes of zeroconf's: no multicast socket is opened."""

from typing import cast

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers import zeroconf as module
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.zeroconf import ZeroconfDiscoveryService


class Browser:
    def __init__(self, zeroconf: object, services: list[str], listener: object):
        self.cancels = 0

    async def async_cancel(self):
        self.cancels += 1


class AsyncZeroconf:
    zeroconf = None

    async def async_close(self):
        pass


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def fakes(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "AsyncZeroconf", AsyncZeroconf)
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "AsyncServiceBrowser", Browser)


async def test_a_registration_cancelled_after_it_stopped_is_gone_already():
    zeroconf = ZeroconfDiscoveryService()
    await zeroconf.start()
    cancel = zeroconf.register(object(), {"_esphomelib._tcp.local."})
    [browser] = cast(set[Browser], zeroconf._browsers)
    await zeroconf.stop()  # before a user that cancels only then

    cancel()
    assert browser.cancels == 1 and zeroconf._adapters == []


================================================================================
# FILE: tests/test_ble_security.py
================================================================================
"""Secure channels: credentials are written to a BLE device only over a link secured first (LE Secure Connections),
through a radio that can pair, or over an unsecured one only when asked for by name."""

import logging
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, Mock

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import (
    BLEConnection,
    BLEPairingError,
    LESecureConnections,
    PairableBLEConnection,
    Unsecured,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.router import BLEService
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakeBLESource


def pairable(calls: list[str] | None = None) -> Mock:
    connection = Mock(spec=PairableBLEConnection)
    connection.pair = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda: calls.append("pair") if calls is not None else None)
    connection.unpair = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda: calls.append("unpair") if calls is not None else None)
    connection.write = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda *_, **__: calls.append("write") if calls is not None else None)
    return connection


async def test_le_secure_connections_pairs_before_any_write_and_unpairs_after():
    calls: list[str] = []
    connection = pairable(calls)

    async with LESecureConnections().secure(connection) as secured:
        await secured.write(1, b"secret")

    assert calls == ["pair", "write", "unpair"]


async def test_le_secure_connections_refuses_a_connection_that_cannot_pair():
    connection = Mock(spec=BLEConnection)

    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="can't pair"):
        async with LESecureConnections().secure(connection):
            pytest.fail("credentials would cross an unencrypted link")
    connection.write.assert_not_called()


async def test_a_failed_pairing_yields_nothing():
    connection = pairable()
    connection.pair.side_effect = BLEPairingError("authentication failed")

    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError):
        async with LESecureConnections().secure(connection):
            pytest.fail("credentials would cross an unencrypted link")
    connection.write.assert_not_called()


async def test_the_bond_is_kept_when_asked():
    connection = pairable()

    async with LESecureConnections(is_pairing_kept=True).secure(connection):
        pass

    connection.unpair.assert_not_called()


async def test_unsecured_writes_as_is_and_says_so(caplog):
    connection = Mock(spec=BLEConnection)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
        async with Unsecured().secure(connection) as secured:
            assert secured is connection
    assert "unencrypted" in caplog.text
    assert not Unsecured.is_pairing_needed and LESecureConnections.is_pairing_needed


@pytest.fixture
async def radios():
    proxy = FakeBLESource("proxy", connection=Mock(spec=BLEConnection))  # stronger, can't pair
    adapter = FakeBLESource("adapter", connection=pairable(), is_pairable=True)
    ble = BLEService(sources=[proxy, adapter])
    await ble.start()
    proxy.advertise("AA", rssi=-40)
    adapter.advertise("AA", rssi=-70)
    yield ble, proxy, adapter
    await ble.stop()


async def test_a_pairing_lease_takes_a_radio_that_can_pair_over_a_stronger_one(radios):
    ble, proxy, adapter = radios

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="test", is_pairing_needed=True) as lease:
        assert lease.source == "adapter"
    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="test") as lease:
        assert lease.source == "proxy"


async def test_a_pairing_lease_fails_when_no_radio_hearing_the_device_can_pair(radios):
    ble, proxy, adapter = radios
    adapter.is_pairable = False

    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="can pair"):
        async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="test", is_pairing_needed=True, timeout=0.1):
            pytest.fail("leased a radio that can't pair")


@pytest.fixture
def adapter_client(monkeypatch):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module

    client = Mock(connect=AsyncMock(), pair=AsyncMock(), unpair=AsyncMock(), address="AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF")
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "BleakClient", lambda *args, **kwargs: client)
    return client


async def test_on_linux_a_local_adapter_pairs_through_its_own_bluez_agent(adapter_client, monkeypatch):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    monkeypatch.setattr(module.sys, "platform", "linux")
    paired = AsyncMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "pair_through_agent", paired)
    adapter = LocalAdapter("hci1")
    assert adapter.is_pairable

    connection = await adapter.connect("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", lambda: None)
    assert isinstance(connection, PairableBLEConnection)
    await connection.pair()
    paired.assert_awaited_once_with("hci1", "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF")
    adapter_client.pair.assert_not_called()  # bleak's brings no agent: Secure Connections fails without one
    await connection.unpair()
    adapter_client.unpair.assert_awaited_once()

    paired.side_effect = ConnectionError("org.bluez.Error.AuthenticationFailed: Authentication Failed")
    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="AuthenticationFailed"):
        await connection.pair()


async def test_elsewhere_the_os_pairs_on_its_own(adapter_client, monkeypatch):
    from bleak.exc import BleakError

    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    monkeypatch.setattr(module.sys, "platform", "darwin")
    connection = await LocalAdapter().connect("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", lambda: None)
    assert isinstance(connection, PairableBLEConnection)

    await connection.pair()
    adapter_client.pair.assert_awaited_once()
    adapter_client.pair.side_effect = BleakError("refused")
    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="refused"):
        await connection.pair()


DEVICE = "/org/bluez/hci0/dev_AA_BB_CC_DD_EE_FF"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("member", "body", "answer"),
    [
        ("RequestAuthorization", [DEVICE], ("", [])),  # Just Works on LE Secure Connections
        ("RequestConfirmation", [DEVICE, 1234], ("", [])),
        ("RequestPasskey", [DEVICE], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("RequestAuthorization", ["/org/bluez/hci0/dev_11_22_33_44_55_66"], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("RequestPinCode", [DEVICE], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("AuthorizeService", [DEVICE, "0000110b-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("Release", [], ("", [])),
    ],
)
def test_the_agent_answers_only_for_the_device_being_paired(member, body, answer):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as bluez_pairing

    assert bluez_pairing.device_path("hci0", "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff") == DEVICE
    assert bluez_pairing.agent_answer(member, body, DEVICE) == answer

# FILE: tests/test_cli.py

"""Exercises the interactive CLI's controller-driving core (`_CliSession`) against a fake
controller wired with the offline test platform — no REPL, no network. The typer-shell
wiring on top is a thin layer over these same calls."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk import Endpoint, IntegrationError, Need, Peripherals
from majordom_integration_sdk.controller import AbstractController
from majordom_integration_sdk.dev.cli import _CliControllerOutput, _CliSession, _print
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.command import DeviceCommand
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import (
    CredentialsType,
    Device,
    DeviceState,
    Discovery,
    ProvidedCredentials,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.event import DeviceParameterChange
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.notification import Notification, NotificationType
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import (
    ParameterDataType,
    ParameterRole,
    ParameterState,
    ParameterVisibility,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import build_test_platform

INTEGRATION = "Fake"


def _param(role: ParameterRole = ParameterRole.control) -> ParameterState:
    return ParameterState(
        id=uuid4(),
        name="On",
        data_type=ParameterDataType.bool,
        role=role,
        visibility=ParameterVisibility.user,
        integration_data=None,
    )


class FakeController(AbstractController):
    """Minimal controller: pairing persists a device with one control parameter; every other
    method just records that it was called with the resolved object."""

    name = INTEGRATION

    def __init__(self, dependencies, *, param_role: ParameterRole = ParameterRole.control):
        super().__init__(dependencies)
        self._discoveries: dict[UUID, Discovery] = {}
        self._param_role = param_role
        self.paired: list[UUID] = []
        self.sent: list[tuple] = []
        self.identified: list[UUID] = []
        self.fetched: list[UUID] = []
        self.unpaired: list[UUID] = []

    @property
    def discoveries(self) -> dict[UUID, Discovery]:
        return self._discoveries

    async def start(self):
        pass

    async def stop(self):
        pass

    async def pair_device(self, discovery: Discovery, credentials: ProvidedCredentials | None):
        device_id = uuid4()
        state = DeviceState(
            id=device_id,
            name=discovery.device_name,
            room_id=uuid4(),
            transport=discovery.transport,
            integration=self.key,
            manufacturer=None,
            parameters=[_param(self._param_role)],
        )
        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
            await repo.save(state)
        self.paired.append(device_id)
        return device_id

    async def unpair(self, device: Device):
        self.unpaired.append(device.id)

    async def identify(self, device: Device):
        self.identified.append(device.id)

    async def fetch(self, device: Device):
        self.fetched.append(device.id)

    async def send_command(self, command: DeviceCommand, device: Device, parameter):
        self.sent.append((command.device_id, command.parameter_id, command.value))


def _discovery() -> Discovery:
    return Discovery(
        id=uuid4(),
        integration=INTEGRATION,
        expected_credentials_options=[CredentialsType.none],
        transport="test",
        device_manufacturer=None,
        device_name="Bulb",
        device_category=None,
        device_icon=None,
    )


@pytest.fixture
def session_and_controller():
    deps = build_test_platform()
    controller = FakeController(deps)
    return _CliSession(controller), controller


async def test_pair_list_control_unpair_flow(session_and_controller):
    session, controller = session_and_controller

    discovery = _discovery()
    controller.discoveries[discovery.id] = discovery

    # pair -> persists a device
    device_id = await session.pair(discovery.id, "none", "")
    assert device_id in controller.paired

    # devices -> lists it
    devices = await session.list_devices()
    assert [d.id for d in devices] == [device_id]

    # device -> shows its (single control) parameter
    state = await session.device_state(device_id)
    assert state is not None
    assert len(state.parameters) == 1
    parameter = state.parameters[0]
    assert parameter.role == ParameterRole.control

    # control -> resolves device+parameter and reaches the controller
    assert await session.control(device_id, parameter.id, True) == "Command sent"
    assert controller.sent == [(device_id, parameter.id, True)]

    # identify / fetch reach the controller with the resolved device
    assert await session.identify(device_id) is True
    assert await session.fetch(device_id) is True
    assert controller.identified == [device_id]
    assert controller.fetched == [device_id]

    # unpair
    assert await session.unpair(device_id) is True
    assert controller.unpaired == [device_id]


async def test_pair_unknown_discovery_returns_none(session_and_controller):
    session, _ = session_and_controller
    assert await session.pair(uuid4()) is None


async def test_actions_on_missing_device(session_and_controller):
    session, controller = session_and_controller
    missing = uuid4()
    assert (await session.control(missing, uuid4(), True)).startswith("No device")
    assert await session.identify(missing) is False
    assert await session.fetch(missing) is False
    assert await session.unpair(missing) is False
    assert controller.sent == controller.identified == []


async def test_control_rejects_non_control_parameter():
    deps = build_test_platform()
    controller = FakeController(deps, param_role=ParameterRole.sensor)
    session = _CliSession(controller)

    discovery = _discovery()
    controller.discoveries[discovery.id] = discovery
    device_id = await session.pair(discovery.id)
    parameter = (await session.device_state(device_id)).parameters[0]

    message = await session.control(device_id, parameter.id, True)
    assert "not controllable" in message
    assert controller.sent == []  # never reached the controller


async def test_output_delegate_persists_event_values():
    deps = build_test_platform()
    controller = FakeController(deps)
    session = _CliSession(controller)

    discovery = _discovery()
    controller.discoveries[discovery.id] = discovery
    device_id = await session.pair(discovery.id)
    parameter = (await session.device_state(device_id)).parameters[0]

    output = _CliControllerOutput()
    await output.controller_did_receive_events(
        controller, [DeviceParameterChange(device_id=device_id, parameter_id=parameter.id, value=True)]
    )

    async with controller.platform.device_repository(controller) as repo:
        stored = await repo.get_parameter_state(device_id, parameter.id)
    assert stored is not None
    assert stored.value  # a (non-empty, encoded) value was written back by the event


async def test_output_delegate_prints_reported_and_resolved_errors(capsys):
    output, controller = _CliControllerOutput(), FakeController(build_test_platform())

    await output.controller_did_encounter_error(controller, IntegrationError("stick-unplugged", "Re-plug it"))
    await output.controller_did_resolve_error(controller, "stick-unplugged")

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "[error] stick-unplugged: Re-plug it" in out and out.rstrip().endswith("[error resolved] stick-unplugged")


async def test_output_delegate_prints_notifications(capsys):
    output, controller = _CliControllerOutput(), FakeController(build_test_platform())
    notification = Notification(message="Firmware update available", type=NotificationType.warning)
    await output.controller_did_emit_notification(controller, notification)
    assert "[notification] warning/normal: Firmware update available" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_prompt_safe_print_is_a_noop_safe_call(capsys):
    # Not a TTY under pytest, so _print falls back to a plain print (no escape codes leaking).
    _print("hello", "world")
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "hello" in out and "world" in out
    assert "\x1b[" not in out  # no cursor-magic when stdout isn't a terminal


def test_run_cli_is_lazily_exported():
    from majordom_integration_sdk import dev

    assert callable(dev.run_cli)


def test_capturing_handler_buffers_then_dumps(capsys):
    import logging

    from majordom_integration_sdk.dev.cli import _CapturingHandler

    handler = _CapturingHandler()
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(levelname)s %(message)s"))
    log = logging.getLogger("test.capture")
    log.addHandler(handler)
    log.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
    log.propagate = False

    log.warning("chatty controller noise")

    # buffered, not printed — the TUI stays clean during the session
    assert capsys.readouterr().err == ""
    assert len(handler.records) == 1

    # dumped to stderr on exit for debugging
    handler.dump()
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "chatty controller noise" in err
    assert "captured logs" in err


# --- needs ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _ZigbeeController(FakeController):
    name = "Fake Zigbee"
    needs = [Need("zigbee", ["ezsp", "znp"]), Need("ble", ["bluez"], is_required=False)]


@pytest.fixture
async def needs_session(tmp_path):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.dev import Runner, build_runtime
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.builtin import silabs_multiprotocol
    from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakeBLERouter, FakeBLESource, FakeCompose, FakePeripheral

    adapter = FakePeripheral(
        "bluetooth-adapters", provides=[Endpoint("ble", "bluez", "hci0", instance=FakeBLESource())]
    )
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("ble", ["router"])])  # runs the router: it takes the adapter
    controller = _ZigbeeController(build_test_platform())
    runtime = build_runtime(
        [controller],
        tmp_path / "runtime",
        runtime_peripherals=[adapter, FakeCompose(), silabs_multiprotocol(), FakeBLERouter(), matter],
        platform=controller.platform,
    )
    runner = Runner(controller, runtime)
    await runner.start()
    yield _CliSession(controller, runtime), runner
    await runner.stop()


async def _until_running(runner, is_running: bool = True):
    async with asyncio.timeout(2):
        while runner.is_running != is_running:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)


async def test_needs_show_what_is_unbound_and_why(needs_session):
    session, runner = needs_session
    assert session.needs() == [
        "zigbee/ezsp|znp  unbound: need zigbee/ezsp|znp: silabs-multiprotocol can't run (need multipan/silabs-cpc: "
        "nothing offers it)",
        "ble/bluez (optional)  unbound: need ble/bluez: every provider taken by ble-router"
        ' — use Need("ble", ["router"])',
    ]
    assert not runner.is_running


async def test_a_pinned_endpoint_binds_the_need_and_starts_the_integration(needs_session):
    session, runner = needs_session
    await session.pin("zigbee", "socket://192.168.1.5:6638")  # the need's first dialect

    assert session.needs()[0] == "zigbee/ezsp|znp  -> socket://192.168.1.5:6638  by pinned"
    await _until_running(runner)
    assert runner.controller.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == Endpoint(
        "zigbee", "ezsp", "socket://192.168.1.5:6638", is_shared=True
    )

    await session.unpin("zigbee")
    assert session.needs()[0].startswith("zigbee/ezsp|znp  unbound")
    assert not runner.is_running
    await session.resolve()  # nothing new: still waiting


async def test_needs_without_a_runtime_list_what_was_given():
    controller = _ZigbeeController(build_test_platform())
    controller.peripherals = Peripherals({"zigbee": Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "/dev/ttyUSB0")})
    session = _CliSession(controller)
    assert session.needs()[0] == "zigbee/ezsp|znp  -> /dev/ttyUSB0  by you"
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="by hand"):
        await session.resolve()

# FILE: tests/test_controller.py
